excerpt.text: { قَالَ قَدْ وَقَعَ } وجب … في أشياء ما هي الا أسماء ليس تحتها مسميات لأنّكم سمّيتموها آلهةً

sources.gloss: 'He said, it has become due' means it has become obligatory ... they are things that are nothing but names with no realities beneath them, because you named them gods.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: { فاذْكُرُوا آلاء اللّهِ } أي نعم الله

sources.gloss: 'So remember the ala of Allah' means the blessings of Allah.

essay.en: This ruku continues al-A'raf's roll of ruined nations, turning first to Salih and then to Lot. Salih is sent to Thamud, 'their brother,' calling them to 'worship Allah' alone. His clear proof is the she-camel: al-Tusi explains that God brought her out of a smooth rock that labored with her as a woman labors in childbirth [5], and that she is called 'this she-camel of Allah' because she had no owner but Him [5]. Salih tells them to let her graze in God's land and not to harm her, on pain of a painful punishment. He then reminds them of God's favor, that He made them successors after Ad and settled them, so that 'you build palaces in its plains, and hew houses out of the mountains.' al-Safi, citing Majma, reports that they carved homes into the mountains because their long lives outlasted ordinary roofs [19]. When the arrogant chiefs confront the weak, al-Mizan notes that these oppressed ones are exactly the believers, and that none of the arrogant believed [1]. They hamstring the she-camel; al-Safi observes that the deed is ascribed to all of them, though only some did it, because it had their consent [19]. They dare Salih to bring the threatened punishment, and 'the earthquake seized them, and they lay lifeless prostrate in their homes.' Salih turns away and addresses the dead, for al-Tusi cites the report that no prophet's community was destroyed while he remained in its midst, so he had withdrawn [10]. The scene shifts to Lot. al-Mizan explains the changed wording by noting that Lot followed the law of Ibrahim, not a law of his own [2]. He confronts his people with an outrage no nation before them had committed [2], coming to men in place of women and exceeding every bound. Their only reply is to expel him, deriding the believers for the very purity that deserved praise [13]. God delivers Lot and his household except his wife, who 'was one of those who remained behind' and perished [14], and rains down stones of sijjil [14]. The account closes as al-A'raf's others do, bidding the reader to 'observe how was the fate of the guilty.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: واما صالح فانه أرسل إلى ثمود وهي قرية واحدة لا تكمل أربعين بيتاً على ساحل البحر صغيرة

text.en: As for Salih, he was sent to Thamud, which was a single small village of fewer than forty houses on the sea coast.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن صالحا (عليه السلام) غاب عن قومه زمانا … فلما رجع إلى قومه لم يعرفوه بصورته، فرجع إليهم و هم على ثلاث طبقات: طبقة جاحدة لا ترجع أبدا، و اخرى شاكة فيه، و اخرى على يقين … و إنما مثل القائم (عليه السلام) مثل صالح (عليه السلام)
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Salih was absent from his people for a time, and when he returned they did not recognize his appearance. He came to them while they were three classes: one denying, that would never turn back; another in doubt; and another of certainty. The likeness of the Qaim is the likeness of Salih.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: لا يدخلن أحد منكم القرية و لا تشربوا من مائهم و لا تدخلوا على هؤلاء المعذبين إلا أن تكونوا باكين أن يصيبكم الذي أصابهم
narrations.chain: Jabir ibn Abdillah

text.en: Let none of you enter the town, nor drink from their water, nor go in upon these punished people unless you are weeping, lest what befell them befall you.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir or al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن إبليس أتاهم في صورة حسنة، فيها تأنيث، عليه ثياب حسنة، فجاء إلى شباب منهم، فأمرهم أن يفعلوا به … فلما وقعوا به التذوه، ثم ذهب عنهم و تركهم، فأحال بعضهم على بعض
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from one of the two Imams

text.en: Iblis came to them in a beautiful form with a feminine cast, in fine clothes, and came to some of their young men and bade them do the act to him. When they did it to him they found it pleasurable; then he departed and left them, and they turned upon one another.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أنّ لوطاً لبث في قومه ثلاثين سنة وكان نازلاً فيهم ولم يكن منهم يدعوهم إلى الله وينهيهم عن الفواحش … وكانوا لا يتطهرون من الجنابة بخلاء أشِحّاء على الطعام فأعقبهم البُخْلُ الداءِ الذي لا دواء له في فروجهم

text.en: Lot dwelt among his people thirty years, a resident though not one of them, calling them to God and forbidding indecencies, but they neither answered nor obeyed. They would not purify themselves after defilement, being miserly and grasping over food; their miserliness left them an incurable disease in their loins.

perspectives.en: On what the passage establishes about the deed of Lot's people, Sunni exegetes draw a legal ruling from it. al-Qurtubi records the jurists' dispute over the penalty, with Malik holding that the offender is stoned whether previously married or not [43], and al-Razi argues that 'the fate of the guilty' makes this particular crime the cause of this particular punishment, still binding in later law [52]. al-Tusi's commentary instead reads the closing 'observe how was the fate of the guilty' not as legislation but as an admonition addressed to everyone accountable, that they reflect and take heed [14].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: المستضعفين هم المؤمنون وأن المؤمنين إنما كانوا من المستضعفين ولم يكن ليؤمن به أحد من المستكبرين

sources.gloss: The oppressed are the believers; the believers were only from among the oppressed, and none of the arrogant believed in him.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والظاهر أن تغيير السياق من جهة أن لوطاً من الأنبياء التابعين لشريعة إبراهيم عليهما السلام لا لشريعة نوح عليه السلام

sources.gloss: Apparently the change of style is because Lot was among the prophets who followed the law of Ibrahim, not the law of Nuh.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والآية التي كانت في الناقة خروجها من صخرة ملساء تمخضت بها كما تتمخض المرأة

sources.gloss: The sign in the she-camel was her coming out of a smooth rock that labored with her as a woman labors in childbirth.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقد روي أنه لم يعذب أمَّة نبي قط ونبيها فيها، فلذلك خرج

sources.gloss: It is reported that no prophet's community was ever punished while its prophet was in its midst, and for that reason he departed.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يتطهرون عن اتيان الرجال في الأدبار فعابوهم بما يجب أن يمدحوا به

sources.gloss: They purify themselves from approaching men, so they blamed them for what deserved praise.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أمر للنبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) والمراد به جميع المكلفين بأن يتفكروا في ذلك ويعلموا كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

sources.gloss: It is a command to the Prophet, but everyone morally accountable is meant by it, that they reflect on this and know how the guilty ended.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فرجع إليهم و هم على ثلاث طبقات: طبقة جاحدة لا ترجع أبدا، و اخرى شاكة فيه، و اخرى على يقين

sources.gloss: He returned to them while they were three classes: one denying that would never turn back, another in doubt, and another of certainty.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لا يدخلن أحد منكم القرية و لا تشربوا من مائهم و لا تدخلوا على هؤلاء المعذبين إلا أن تكونوا باكين أن يصيبكم الذي أصابهم

sources.gloss: Let none of you enter the town, nor drink their water, nor go in upon these punished people unless you are weeping, lest what befell them befall you.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن إبليس أتاهم في صورة حسنة، فيها تأنيث، عليه ثياب حسنة، فجاء إلى شباب منهم، فأمرهم أن يفعلوا به

sources.gloss: Iblis came to them in a beautiful form with a feminine cast, in fine clothes, and came to some of their young men and bade them do the act to him.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: اسند العقر إلى جميعهم وان لم يعقرها الا بعضهم لأنّه كان برضاهم

sources.gloss: The hamstringing is ascribed to all of them, though only some did it, because it was with their consent.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أنّ لوطاً لبث في قومه ثلاثين سنة وكان نازلاً فيهم ولم يكن منهم يدعوهم إلى الله وينهيهم عن الفواحش

sources.gloss: Lot dwelt among his people thirty years, a resident though not one of them, calling them to God and forbidding indecencies.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: فقال مالك: يُرْجَم أحْصِن أو لم يُحصَن

sources.gloss: Malik said: he is stoned, whether previously married or not.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: فهذه الآية تقتضي كون هذا الجرم المخصوص علة لحصول هذا الزاجر المخصوص

sources.gloss: This verse entails that this particular crime is the cause of this particular deterrent.

essay.en:
Shu'ayb is sent to Midian, and like the messengers before him in this sura he opens with the oneness of God and the call to worship Him alone. He tells them a manifest proof has come from their Lord. Al-Tusi notes the objection that the Quran names no miracle for Shu'ayb, and answers, with al-Zajjaj, that the verse makes the command to observe the measure follow upon that proof, so a sign of his prophethood must have come, even if it goes unnamed [5].

His people short-changed one another, so he commands full measure and weight and forbids cheating people of their goods [2]. He forbids corruption after the land's restoration, which al-Mizan nearly restricts to what strips away public safety in property, honor and life [1]. He warns them not to sit on every road to threaten and turn believers back, and to remember that they were once few and He multiplied them.

The arrogant among the elite, who raised themselves above their true measure, threaten to expel Shu'ayb and the faithful or force them back to 'our creed' - supposing he had once shared their religion, though he had kept it concealed [3]. He answers that to return would be to fabricate a lie against God, and he entrusts the verdict to God, the best of judges. The faithless elite then warn the people that following him means loss.

The earthquake seizes them, and they lie lifeless in their homes. Al-Tabrisi records the view that Shu'ayb had two peoples, one destroyed by the quake and one by the day of the canopy [4]. Those who denied Shu'ayb became as if they had never lived there, and their own taunt is turned back: they, not the believers, were the losers [4]. Shu'ayb turns away as one who has lost hope for them, having delivered his Lord's messages and counseled them, and asks how he should grieve for a faithless people [13].

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: فكانوا إخوانهم في دينهم أو في عشيرتهم؟ قال له الرجل: بل في عشيرتهم. قال: فهؤلاء إخوانهم في عشيرتهم، و ليسوا إخوانهم في دينهم
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Yahya ibn al-Musawir al-Hamdani, from his father

text.en: So were they their brothers in religion, or in their tribe? The man said: In their tribe. He said: Then they were their brothers in tribe, and not their brothers in religion.

narrations.speaker: The Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: و كان رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) إذا ذكر شعيبا يقول: ذاك خطيب الأنبياء لحسن مراجعته قومه
narrations.chain: from Ibn Abbas

text.en: The Messenger of God, whenever he mentioned Shu'ayb, would say: 'That is the orator of the prophets,' for the excellence of how he addressed his people.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أما شعيب فإنه أرسل إلى مدين، و هي لا تكمل أربعين بيتا

text.en: As for Shu'ayb, he was sent to Midian, and it did not amount to forty houses.

note.en: Al-Tusi cites al-Balkhi: here Shu'ayb ordered them to stop barring people from the faith and threatening them, which is right, not to persist in disbelief; so not every act of the faithless is disbelief [7].

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Mu'minin
narrations.arabic: و كان أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) يقول: إذا لقي العدو محاربا … اللهم إنا نشكو إليك غيبة نبينا، و كثرة عدونا، و تشتت أهوائنا ربنا افتح بيننا و بين قومنا بالحق و أنت خير الفاتحين

text.en: When Amir al-Mu'minin met an enemy in battle he would say: ... O God, we complain to You of the absence of our prophet, the multitude of our foes, and the scattering of our desires. Our Lord, judge justly between us and our people; You are the best of judges.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: بَعَث الله عليهم الصيحة الواحدة فماتوا

text.en: God sent upon them the single blast, and they died.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: مقابلته لما قبله وما بعده يخصه - تقريباً - بالإِفساد الذي يسلب الأمن العام في الأموال والأعراض والنفوس كقطع الطرق ونهب الأموال وهتك الأعراض وقتل النفوس المحترمة

sources.gloss: Its pairing with what comes before and after nearly restricts 'corruption' to what removes public security in property, honor and lives, such as highway robbery, plunder, violating honor, and killing protected persons.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فأوفوا الكيل والميزان أي أتموا ما تكيلونه على الناس بالمكيال وما تزنونه عليهم بالميزان … ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم أي لا تنقصوهم حقوقهم

sources.gloss: 'Observe the measure and the balance' means complete for people what you measure and weigh out to them; 'do not cheat people of their goods' means do not diminish their rights.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال الملأَ الذين استكبروا من قومه أي رفعوا أنفسهم فوق مقدارها … لأَنه كان عندهم وفي ظنّهم أنه كان قبل ذلك على دينهم فلذلك أطلقوا لفظ العود وقد كان ع يخفي دينه فيهم

sources.gloss: 'The elite who were arrogant' means they raised themselves above their measure; they used the word 'return' because they supposed he had earlier been on their religion, while he had concealed his religion among them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل: إنه كان لشعيب قومان قوم أهلكوا بالرجفة وقوم هم أصحاب الظلة

sources.gloss: It is said that Shu'ayb had two peoples: one destroyed by the earthquake and one who were the people of the canopy.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال الفراء: لم يكن لشعيب آية على النبوة. قال الزجاج وغيره: هذا غلط، لأنه قال { قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم فأوفوا } فجاء بالفاء جواباً للجزاء

sources.gloss: Al-Farra said Shu'ayb had no sign of prophethood. Al-Zajjaj and others said this is an error, for the verse says 'a manifest proof has come to you from your Lord, so observe,' bringing the fa as the answer to the condition.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال البلخي: أمرهم في هذه الآية بالكف عما كانوا يفعلون من الصد عن الدين والتوعد عليه، والكف عن ذلك خير ورشد، ولم يأمرهم بالمقام على كفرهم … وفي ذلك دلالة على أنه ليس كل أفعال الكافرين كفراً ومعصية

sources.gloss: Al-Balkhi said: in this verse he ordered them to desist from barring people from the religion and threatening over it, and desisting is good and right; he did not order them to remain in their disbelief. This shows that not every act of the disbelievers is disbelief and sin.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أنه تولى عنهم ومعناه أعرض عنهم إِعراض آيس منهم

sources.gloss: He turned away from them, meaning he averted himself from them as one who had despaired of them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فكانوا إخوانهم في دينهم أو في عشيرتهم؟ قال له الرجل: بل في عشيرتهم. قال: فهؤلاء إخوانهم في عشيرتهم، و ليسوا إخوانهم في دينهم

sources.gloss: Were they their brothers in religion or in tribe? The man said: In their tribe. He said: Then they were their brothers in tribe, not their brothers in religion.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و كان رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) إذا ذكر شعيبا يقول: ذاك خطيب الأنبياء لحسن مراجعته قومه

sources.gloss: The Messenger of God, whenever he mentioned Shu'ayb, would say: 'That is the orator of the prophets,' for the excellence of how he addressed his people.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وفي المجمع عن الصادق عليه السلام بَعَث الله عليهم الصيحة الواحدة فماتوا

sources.gloss: In Majma, from al-Sadiq: God sent upon them the single blast, and they died.

essay.en: The passage gathers the prophet-stories just told into a law of history. No prophet is sent to a town without its people being visited with stress and distress, so that they might entreat their Lord. Tusi reads this as a tightening of the trial to soften hard hearts, done because God knows the welfare in it for them [4]. When hardship fails to move them, God swaps it for ease: the ill conditions turn to good until the people multiply, and instead of learning they shrug that adversity and ease befell their fathers too, as if this were only the turning of time [2]. So He seizes them suddenly, unaware, which Tusi explains falls after ease to make the grief greater [5]. Tabatabai frames this ease as istidraj, a gradual drawing toward punishment: the bad turned to good, hardship to ease, until He seizes them suddenly [1]. Verse 96 names the hinge: had the townsfolk believed and been Godwary, blessings of heaven and earth, rain above and growth below, would have opened to them; but they denied, and were seized for what they earned [6]. The passage closes in warning questions. Do the townsfolk feel secure from punishment reaching them asleep at night, or at play at midday? Do they feel secure from God's devising? For Tusi, devising ascribed to God is His punishment, seizing the servant from where he does not perceive [8]; Qummi says God's devising here is the punishment [9]. Only the losers feel safe.

narrations.speaker: The Prophet
narrations.arabic: أكرموا الخبز، فإن الله أنزله من بركات السماء، و أخرجه من بركات الأرض
narrations.chain: from Musa al-Ta'ifi

text.en: Honor bread, for God sent it down from the blessings of heaven and brought it out from the blessings of the earth.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: صليت خلف أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام) فأطرق، ثم قال … اللهم لا تؤمني مكرك
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Safwan al-Jammal

text.en: I prayed behind Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq; he lowered his head, then said: O God, do not make me feel secure from Your devising.

perspectives.en: On why God visits a town with hardship 'so that they might entreat,' the traditions divide over whether God's acts can carry a purpose. Tusi reads the phrase as fully purposive: God afflicts them because He knows the welfare in it for them, and 'la'alla' here means 'in order that' they entreat [4]. Razi reports the Mu'tazila taking the verse as proof that God wills faith and obedience from every accountable person, while his own Ash'ari school holds that assigning a cause to God's acts is impossible, so the verse means only that God did what, done by another, would resemble a purpose [23].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ثم تتبعها سنة ثالثة وهي الاستدراج، وهي بتبديل السيئة حسنة، والنقمة نعمة والبأساء والضراء، سراء، وفي ذلك تقريبهم يوماً فيوماً وساعة فساعة إلى العذاب الإِلهي حتى يأخذهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون به

sources.gloss: Then a third divine way follows, istidraj: turning the bad into good, punishment into blessing, hardship and adversity into ease, drawing them nearer day by day and hour by hour to the divine chastisement until He seizes them suddenly, while they do not perceive it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي قال بعضهم لبعض هكذا عادة الدهر فكونوا على ما أنتم عليه كما كان آباؤكم كذلك

sources.gloss: That is, they said to one another: this is the way of time, so remain as you are, as your fathers were likewise.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وانما يفعل بهم ذلك لعلمه بما لهم فيه من الصلاح لكي يتضرعوا … ان يكون (لعل) بمعنى اللام وتقديره ليضرعوا

sources.gloss: He does that to them only because He knows the welfare in it for them, so that they might humble themselves ... and 'la'alla' here has the sense of 'in order that,' meaning so that they might entreat.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فاذا فسدوا على الامرين جميعا اخذهم بغتة ليكون ذلك اعظم في الحسرة

sources.gloss: So when they become corrupt on both counts, He seizes them suddenly, so that it is greater in grief.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فبركات السماء بالقطر، وبركات الارض بالنبات والثمار

sources.gloss: The blessings of heaven are by rain, and the blessings of earth are by plants and fruits.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: انما جاز اضافة المكر الى الله لما في ذلك من المبالغة … لانه اخذ للعبد بالضِّر من حيث لا يشعر

sources.gloss: Ascribing devising to God is permissible only for the emphasis in it ... because it is a seizing of the servant with harm from where he does not perceive.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: المكر من الله العذاب

sources.gloss: Devising from God is the punishment.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أكرموا الخبز، فإن الله أنزله من بركات السماء، و أخرجه من بركات الأرض

sources.gloss: Honor bread, for God sent it down from the blessings of heaven and brought it out from the blessings of the earth.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: اللهم لا تؤمني مكرك

sources.gloss: O God, do not make me feel secure from Your devising.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: قالت المعتزلة: وهذا يدل على أنه تعالى أراد من كل المكلفين الإيمان والطاعة. وقال أصحابنا: لما ثبت بالدليل أن تعليل أفعال الله وأحكامه محال

sources.gloss: The Mu'tazila said: this shows that God willed faith and obedience from all the accountable. Our companions said: since it is established by proof that assigning a cause to God's acts and rulings is impossible...

essay.en:
The passage closes the account of the ruined towns, then opens the story of Moses. Verse 100 asks whether it has not dawned on those who inherit the earth after earlier peoples that God, if He willed, could seize them for their sins and seal their hearts so they no longer hear. Tabrisi reads the opening question as an affirmation: has God not made this clear? [3] Tabatabai treats these verses as a summary of how the bygone nations, most of whom broke the divine covenant, fell under a succession of divine customs following one upon another. [1]

Verse 101 tells the Prophet that these towns' accounts are recounted to him so his people may take heed [6]; their messengers came with clear proofs, yet they would not believe in what they had denied earlier. Verse 102 finds in most of them no covenant kept, which Tusi explains as what God set in their reason, the duty to thank the Benefactor, or the pledge given through the prophets to worship Him alone [7].

Verse 103 turns: after them God sent Moses with His signs to Pharaoh and his elite, but they wronged them. Tabatabai notes the shift in style marks a fresh stage, for Moses is one of the resolute messengers, bringing a book and a law [2]; their wronging means they wronged themselves by denying the signs [8]. Moses declares himself an apostle of the Lord of all the worlds, bound to say only the truth, and asks that the Children of Israel be released, which Tusi reads as freeing them from the hard labor Pharaoh had bound them to [10]. Pharaoh demands the sign, out of denial and doubt that it could be real [11]. Moses casts his staff and it becomes a manifest python, and draws out his hand, white to the onlookers; Tusi notes the great serpent, and that Moses himself was dark-skinned, so the whiteness stood out [12]. The passage leaves the reader at the edge of the contest to come.

note.en: Qummi glosses 'what they had denied earlier' as their denial in the primordial realm of particles, the dharr, and a refutation of those who reject that first covenant [14].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن الله عز و جل خلق الخلق … ثم بعثهم في الظلال … ثم بعث منهم النبيين فدعوهم إلى الإقرار بالله عز و جل … ثم دعوهم إلى الإقرار بالنبيين، فأقر بعض و أنكر بعض، ثم دعوهم إلى ولايتنا، فأقر بها و الله من أحب، و أنكرها من أبغض، و هو قوله: { فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ بِهِ مِن قَبْلُ } … كان التكذيب ثم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi and Uqba, both from Abu Ja'far

text.en: God created creation, making those He loved from the clay of the Garden and those He disliked from the clay of the Fire. He raised them as shadows, then called them to affirm God, then the prophets, then our wilayah: whoever He loved affirmed it, whoever He disliked denied it. The denial was there.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إنّكم وفيتم بما أخذ الله عليه ميثاقكم من ولايتنا، وإنّكم لم تبدّلوا بنا غيرنا، ولو لم تفعلوا لعيّركم الله كما عيّرهم، حيث يقول جلّ ذكره: (وَمَا وَجَدْنَا لاِكْثَرِهِمْ مِنْ عَهْد وَإِنْ وَجَدْنَا أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَفَاسِقِينَ)
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father Sulayman al-Daylami

text.en: You have fulfilled the covenant God took from you concerning our wilayah, and you have never exchanged us for another. Had you not, God would have reproached you as He reproached them, saying, 'We did not find in most of them any covenant, and We found most of them to be transgressors.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ كَانَ مُؤْمِناً وَأَحَبَّ أَنْ يَزْدَادَ إِيمَاناً وَأَنْتَ شَاكٌّ وَالشَّاكُّ لا خَيْرَ فِيهِ … إِنَّ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَقُولُ وَما وَجَدْنا لأكْثَرِهِمْ مِنْ عَهْدٍ وَإِنْ وَجَدْنا أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَفاسِقِينَ قَالَ نَزَلَتْ فِي الشَّاكِّ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hakam

text.en: Ibrahim was a believer who wished to increase his faith; but you are a doubter, and there is no good in the doubter. God says, 'We did not find in most of them any covenant, and We found most of them to be transgressors' - it was revealed about the doubter.

perspectives.en: Both traditions trace 'what they had denied earlier' and the broken covenant back to the primordial pledge taken from the descendants of Adam. The Shia narrations add that what was affirmed or denied at that pledge included the wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt, so denial in this world only carries forward the denial made there [16]. Sunni commentators tie the same words to that covenant: Ibn Kathir to the pledge taken in the loins that God is the sole Lord [28], and Tabari, from al-Suddi, that they believed then only under compulsion and so would not believe now [21].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وهي تلخص القول في قصص الأمم الغابرة فتذكر أن أكثرهم كانوا فاسقين خارجين عن زي العبودية لم يفوا بالعهد الإِلهي والميثاق الذي أُخذ منهم لأول يوم، وتبين أن ذلك كان هو السبب في وقوعهم في مجرى سنن خاصة إلهية يتبع بعضها بعضاً

sources.gloss: These verses summarize the account of the bygone nations, noting that most of them were transgressors who did not keep the divine covenant and pledge taken from them at the first, and that this was why they fell under a chain of special divine laws following one upon another.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: في تغيير السياق في أول القصة دلالة على تجدد الاهتمام بأمر موسى عليه السلام فإنه من أُولي العزم صاحب كتاب وشريعة

sources.gloss: The change of style at the opening of the story indicates renewed concern with the matter of Moses, for he is one of the resolute messengers, possessor of a book and a law.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { أو لم يهد } وهو استفهام يراد به التقرير أي أو لم يُبيّن الله

sources.gloss: 'Does it not guide' is a question meant as affirmation, that is: has God not made it clear?

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أخبر الله تعالى عن اهل القرى التي ذكرها وقص خبرها واشار بـ { تلك } اليها، لانه خاطب النبي … يعني قصص انباء القرى ما فيه من الاعتبار

sources.gloss: God tells of the people of the towns He mentioned and points to them with 'these,' for He addresses the Prophet, meaning the accounts of the towns, with the admonition they contain.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: الله تعالى اخذ عليهم العهد بما جعله في عقولهم من وجوب شكر المنعم والقيام بحق المنعم … وقيل العهد ما عهد اليهم مع الانبياء ان يعبدوه ولا يشركوا به شيئا

sources.gloss: God took the covenant from them by what He placed in their minds, the duty to thank the Benefactor and fulfill His right; and it is said the covenant is what was enjoined on them through the prophets: to worship Him and associate nothing with Him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله { فظلموا بها } معناه ظلموا أنفسم بجحدها

sources.gloss: His words 'they wronged them' mean they wronged themselves by denying them, the signs.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله { فأرسل معي بني إسرائيل } خطاب من موسى لفرعون، وأمره اياه أن يخلي عن بني اسرائيل من اعتقاله، لانه كان قد اعتقلهم للاستخدام في الاعمال الشاقة

sources.gloss: 'So let the Children of Israel go with me' is Moses's address to Pharaoh, ordering him to release the Children of Israel from his detention, for he had held them for hard labor.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أي هات بها { إن كنت } صادقا { من الصادقين } على طريق اليأس منه بذلك وجهله بصحته وامكانه

sources.gloss: 'Produce it,' that is, bring it, 'if you are' truthful 'of the truthful': by way of his despair of it and his ignorance of its validity and possibility.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فالثعبان هو الحية الضخمة الطويلة … وكان موسى (ع) أسمر شديد السمرة

sources.gloss: The thu'ban is the huge, long serpent; and Moses was brown, of intense brownness, dark-complexioned.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: { فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا من قبل } في الذر الأول قال: لا يؤمنون في الدنيا بما كذبوا في الذر الأول وهي رد على من أنكر الميثاق في الذر الأول

sources.gloss: 'They would not believe in what they denied earlier,' in the first realm of particles, the dharr; he said: they do not believe in this world in what they denied in the first dharr, and this is a refutation of whoever denies the covenant of the first dharr.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ثم دعوهم إلى ولايتنا، فأقر بها و الله من أحب، و أنكرها من أبغض، و هو قوله: { فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ بِهِ مِن قَبْلُ }

sources.gloss: Then He called them to our wilayah; whoever He loved affirmed it, whoever He disliked denied it, and that is His saying, 'they would not believe in what they had denied before.'

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: { فَمَا كانُوا لِـيُؤْمِنُوا بِـمَا كَذّبُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ } قال: ذلك يوم أخذ منهم الـميثاق فآمنوا كُرْهاً

sources.gloss: al-Suddi: 'they would not believe in what they denied earlier' means that was the day their covenant was taken and they believed under compulsion.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: والعهد الذي أخذه هو ما جبلهم عليه، وفطرهم عليه، وأخذ عليهم في الأصلاب أنه ربهم ومليكهم، وأنه لا إله إلا هو

sources.gloss: The covenant He took is what He made their nature upon and took from them in the loins: that He is their Lord and King, and that there is no god but He.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: إنّكم وفيتم بما أخذ الله عليه ميثاقكم من ولايتنا، وإنّكم لم تبدّلوا بنا غيرنا، ولو لم تفعلوا لعيّركم الله كما عيّرهم، حيث يقول جلّ ذكره: (وَمَا وَجَدْنَا لاِكْثَرِهِمْ مِنْ عَهْد وَإِنْ وَجَدْنَا أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَفَاسِقِينَ)

sources.gloss: You fulfilled the covenant God took from you concerning our wilayah, and you never exchanged us for another; had you not, God would have reproached you as He reproached them, saying, 'We did not find in most of them any covenant, and We found most of them transgressors.'

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ كَانَ مُؤْمِناً وَأَحَبَّ أَنْ يَزْدَادَ إِيمَاناً وَأَنْتَ شَاكٌّ وَالشَّاكُّ لا خَيْرَ فِيهِ … قَالَ نَزَلَتْ فِي الشَّاكِّ

sources.gloss: Ibrahim was a believer who wished to increase his faith; but you are a doubter, and there is no good in the doubter; it was revealed about the doubter.

essay.en:
Al-Mizan marks a shift in the sura's style as Moses' story begins: he is the third of the resolute messengers, bringing a new scripture and a new law [1]. The passage opens after his two signs, the staff and the shining hand, have already unsettled the court.

Pharaoh's chiefs, whom the Quran calls 'the elite' (al-mala'), a word al-Tibyan ties to the awe of them that fills the breast [6], pronounce Moses 'an expert magician' bent on driving them from their land. They counsel Pharaoh to put Moses and his brother off and to send heralds through the cities to gather every skilled magician. The magicians arrive and bargain: will they have a reward if they win? Pharaoh promises reward and a place among those near him, a promise Majma al-Bayan reads as a mark of his own weakness, since he needed the magicians only for his incapacity [3].

At the contest the magicians invite Moses to throw first; he tells them to throw, and they bewitch the people's eyes and overawe them with a tremendous magic. Then God signals Moses to cast his staff, and it swallows their fabrications. The truth comes out, their work is undone, and they are vanquished and humiliated. What they had witnessed, Majma notes, no rational person could ascribe to human power, so they acknowledged God's oneness and prophethood [4]: the magicians fall prostrate, declaring faith in the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.

Pharaoh rounds on them, calling their faith a plot devised in the city and threatening to cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify them all, the first ruler, Majma reports, to inflict such a punishment [5]. The magicians answer that they are returning to their Lord, and that he resents them only for believing. They close by asking God to pour patience upon them, the grace to endure Pharaoh's cruelty, al-Tibyan explains [14], and to let them die as Muslims.

narrations.speaker: the Imam
narrations.arabic: إن موسى و هارون (عليهما السلام) حين دخلا على فرعون لم يكن في جلسائه يومئذ ولد سفاح، كانوا ولد نكاح كلهم، و لو كان فيهم ولد سفاح لأمر بقتلهما، فقالوا: أَرْجِهْ وَ أَخَاهُ … ثم وضع يده على صدره، و قال: و كذلك نحن، لا ينزع إلينا إلا كل خبيث الولادة
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Yunus ibn Zabyan

text.en: When Moses and Aaron came before Pharaoh, not one of his courtiers that day was base-born; all were of lawful birth. Had a bastard been present, he would have ordered the two killed. So they said, 'Put him and his brother off.' Then, hand on his chest: 'So are we; none inclines to us but the vile-born.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أشهد أن المرجئة على دين الذين قالوا: { أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِي ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَاشِرِينَ }
narrations.chain: Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: I bear witness that the Murji'a follow the religion of those who said, 'Put him and his brother off, and send heralds to the cities.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: كانت عصا موسى لآدم فصارت إلى شعيب، ثم صارت إلى موسى بن عمران، و إنها لتروع و تلقف ما يأفكون، و تصنع ما تؤمر، يفتح لها شعبتان إحداهما في الأرض و الاخرى في السقف، و بينهما أربعون ذراعا تلقف ما يأفكون بلسانها
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Muhammad ibn Ali

text.en: The staff of Moses belonged to Adam, then passed to Shu'ayb, then to Moses son of Imran. It terrifies and swallows what they fake and does what it is bidden. Two branches open for it, one in the ground, one in the ceiling, forty cubits apart, swallowing their falsehood with its tongue.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: كن لما لا ترجو أرجى منك لما ترجوا … و خرجت سحرة فرعون يطلبون العزة لفرعون فرجعوا مؤمنين
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Amir al-Muminin

text.en: Be more hopeful of what you do not hope for than of what you do hope for. … Pharaoh's magicians went out seeking might for Pharaoh, and came back believers.

perspectives.en: On 'the magicians fell down in prostration,' the passive verb 'were cast down' carries a doctrinal weight. Razi reports that his fellow Ash'aris argued from it that another cast them prostrate, none but God, the Lord of the worlds, so that a servant's act is God's own creation [45]. Al-Tibyan reads the same passive differently: the overwhelming signs left the magicians unable to hold back, yet this was not compulsion to faith, for had they been forced they would deserve no praise; they believed by proof, recognizing what no human power could produce [11].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: لأنه ثالث أُولي العزم صاحب كتاب جديد وشريعة جديدة

sources.gloss: because he is the third of the resolute messengers, possessor of a new scripture and a new law.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لم يحتج إلى السحرة إلاّ لعجزه وضعفه

sources.gloss: he needed the magicians only on account of his incapacity and weakness.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وكل من هذه الأمور يعلم كل عاقل أنه لا يدخل تحت مقدور البشر فاعترفوا بالتوحيد والنبوة

sources.gloss: every rational person knows that none of these matters falls within human power, so they acknowledged God's oneness and prophethood.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: إن أول من قطع الرجل وصلب فرعون

sources.gloss: the first to cut off a foot and to crucify was Pharaoh.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لأنه يملأ الصدر هيبتهم

sources.gloss: the elite are called al-mala' because the awe of them fills the breast.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ولم يكن ذلك على وجه الاضطرار الى الايمان، لأنه لو كان كذلك لما مدحوا عليه

sources.gloss: this was not compulsion to faith, for had it been so they would not be praised for it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: سألوا الله تعالى أن يفرغ عليهم صبراً، ومعناه أن يفعل بهم من اللطف ما يصبرون معه على عذاب فرعون

sources.gloss: they asked God to pour patience upon them, meaning that He grant them the grace to endure Pharaoh's punishment.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أشهد أن المرجئة على دين الذين قالوا: { أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِي ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَاشِرِينَ }

sources.gloss: I bear witness that the Murji'a are on the religion of those who said, 'Put him and his brother off, and send heralds to the cities.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: كانت عصا موسى لآدم فصارت إلى شعيب، ثم صارت إلى موسى بن عمران

sources.gloss: the staff of Moses belonged to Adam, then passed to Shu'ayb, then to Moses son of Imran.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: احتج أصحابنا بقوله تعالى: { وَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سَـٰجِدِينَ } قالوا: دلت هذه الآية على أن غيرهم ألقاهم ساجدين، وما ذاك إلا الله رب العالمين فهذا يدل على أن فعل العبد خلق الله تعالى

sources.gloss: our colleagues argued from 'the magicians were cast down prostrate' that another cast them down, none but God, which shows that a servant's act is God's creation.

essay.en:
The passage turns from Pharaoh's beaten magicians to his court. The elite press Pharaoh, warning that Moses and his people will spread corruption and that Moses will abandon Pharaoh and his gods. By 'corruption' they mean that Moses is calling people to reject Pharaoh's worship, which threatens his rule [4]. Pharaoh answers that he will kill their sons and spare their women, and that he stays dominant over them. Al-Tabrisi notes that he no longer hoped to reach Moses himself, given his standing, so he turned back against the weak of Bani Israil as he had before [2]. The words 'and your gods' show that Pharaoh, though claiming lordship, also had gods of his own, which al-Mizan takes as worship of other gods even while he enslaved people to himself [1]; on a reading traced to Ali the word is 'your worship' [12].

Moses answers his frightened people: turn to Allah and be patient, for the earth belongs to Allah, who gives its inheritance to whom He wills, and the outcome is for the Godwary. Al-Tusi reads this as both consolation, since the land passes from nation to nation, and hope that they will inherit Pharaoh's land [5]. When they complain of torment before and after his coming, Moses renews the promise; al-Tabrisi holds that 'maybe' from Allah is binding, and that God fulfilled it, settling Bani Israil in the land [3].

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: كان فرعون يعبد الأصنام ثم ادعى بعد ذلك الربوبية، فقال فرعون

text.en: Pharaoh used to worship idols, then afterward he claimed lordship; and it was Pharaoh himself who gave the reply that followed.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وجدنا في كتاب علي (عليه السلام) … أنا و أهل بيتي الذين أورثنا الأرض، و نحن المتقون، و الأرض كلها لنا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, by his chain from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Abu Jafar

text.en: We found in the book of Ali: I and my Ahl al-Bayt are those whom Allah made inherit the earth; we are the Godwary, and the whole earth is ours.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أيها الناس، أين تذهبون؟ و أين يراد بكم؟ بنا هدى الله أولكم، و بنا يختم الله آخركم، فإن يكن لكم ملك معجل، فإن لنا ملكا مؤجلا، و ليس بعد ملكنا ملك، لأنها أهل العاقبة، يقول الله عز و جل … وَٱلْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mualla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Salih ibn Hamza, from his father, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami

text.en: O people, where are you going? Where are you being driven? By us Allah guided your first, and by us Allah seals your last. If you have a hastened kingdom, ours is a deferred kingdom, and after our kingdom there is no kingdom, for we are the people of the outcome. Allah says: 'The outcome is for the Godwary.'

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: قال الذين آمنوا يا موسى قد أوذينا قبل مجيئك بقتل أولادنا ومن بعد ما جئتنا لما حبسهم فرعون لإيمانهم بموسى … ومعنى ينظر أي: يرى كيف تعملون فوضع النظر مكان الرؤية

text.en: Those who believed said: O Moses, we were harmed before your coming by the killing of our children, and after you came, when Pharaoh imprisoned them for believing in Moses. 'He will look' here means He sees how you act; 'looking' stands for 'seeing.'

perspectives.en: On verse 129 the Shia commentators read the complaint as impatience under renewed oppression: al-Tusi takes 'before you came' as Pharaoh's killing of the sons and enslaving of the women, and 'after you came' as his fresh threat to repeat that torment, so the people were pressing Moses for the rescue he had promised [6]. Al-Tabari keeps this reading but adds a second occasion, from al-Suddi and Ibn Abbas: Bani Israil said it when Pharaoh's army overtook them at the sea and they feared they were caught [16]. Both hold that Moses answered by renewing God's promise.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وفيه دلالة على أن فرعون كما كان يدعي الألوهية، ويستعبد الناس لنفسه كان يعبد آلهة أُخرى

sources.gloss: In it is an indication that Pharaoh, just as he claimed divinity and enslaved the people to himself, also worshipped other gods.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وإن كان فرعون قد انقطع طمعه عن قتل موسى وقومه فلم يقل سأقتل موسى وقومه لما رأى من علّو أمره وعظم شأنه فانتقل إلى عذاب المستضعفين منهم وهم أبناء بني إسرائيل

sources.gloss: Although Pharaoh had lost hope of killing Moses and his people, so he did not say 'I will kill Moses and his people,' seeing the height of his affair and his great standing, he turned instead to punishing the weak among them, the sons of Bani Israil.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال الزجاج: عسى طمع واشفاق إلا أن ما يطمع الله فيه فهو واجب … وقد حقّق الله سبحانه هذا الوعد فأورث بني إسرائيل أرض مصر ونواحيها بعد أن أهلك عدوَّهم

sources.gloss: Al-Zajjaj said: 'maybe' is hope and apprehension, except that what Allah gives hope of is binding. And Allah realized this promise: He made Bani Israil inherit the land of Egypt and its regions after He destroyed their enemy.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وعنوا بالافساد في الارض دعاء الخلق الى مخالفة فرعون في عبادته وتجهيله إِياه في ديانته لما يتفق عليه من ذلك مما لا قبل له به مما فيه انتقاض أمره وبطلان ملكه

sources.gloss: By 'corruption in the land' they meant his calling the people to oppose Pharaoh in his worship and to declare his religion ignorance, since that would lead to the undoing of his authority and the collapse of his kingship.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أحدهما - التسلية لهم بأنها لا تبقي على أحد لانها تنقل من قوم الى قوم اما محنة او عقوبة. الثاني - الاطماع في ان يورثهم الله ارض فرعون وقومه

sources.gloss: The first is consolation for them, that the land does not remain with anyone, for it passes from people to people, whether as a trial or a punishment. The second is giving them hope that Allah will make them inherit the land of Pharaoh and his people.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والاذى الذي كان بهم قيل: هو استعباد فرعون اياهم وقتل ابنائهم واستحياء نسائهم للاستخدام. والذي كان بعد مجيء موسى الوعيد لهم بتجديد ذلك العذاب … وكان هذا على سبيل الاستبطاء منهم لما وعدهم فجدد الوعد لهم وحققه

sources.gloss: The harm that befell them, it is said, was Pharaoh's enslaving them, killing their sons, and keeping their women alive for service; and what came after Moses arrived was the threat of renewing that torment. This was by way of their impatience for what he had promised, so he renewed the promise for them and confirmed it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: كان فرعون يعبد الأصنام ثم ادعى بعد ذلك الربوبية، فقال فرعون

sources.gloss: Pharaoh used to worship idols, then afterward he claimed lordship. So Pharaoh said...

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال الذين آمنوا يا موسى قد أوذينا قبل مجيئك بقتل أولادنا ومن بعد ما جئتنا لما حبسهم فرعون لإيمانهم بموسى

sources.gloss: Those who believed said: O Moses, we were harmed before your coming by the killing of our children, and after you came, when Pharaoh imprisoned them for their faith in Moses.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أنا و أهل بيتي الذين أورثنا الأرض، و نحن المتقون، و الأرض كلها لنا

sources.gloss: I and my Ahl al-Bayt are those whom Allah made inherit the earth, and we are the Godwary, and the whole earth is ours.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وفي المجمع عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام أنّه قرء ويدرك والا هتك يعني عبادتك

sources.gloss: And in al-Majma, from Amir al-Muminin, that he recited 'and he abandons you and your worship,' meaning your worship.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وقـيـل: إن قوم موسى قالوا لـموسى ذلك حين خافوا أن يدركهم فرعون وهم منه هاربون، وقد تراءى الـجمعان

sources.gloss: It is said that Moses' people said this to him when they feared Pharaoh would overtake them as they fled from him, and the two hosts had come within sight of one another.

essay.en:
This passage tracks God's judgment on Pharaoh's clan and what followed for the Children of Israel. It opens by recalling that He afflicted Pharaoh's people with droughts and loss of produce, so that they may take admonition [3]. Yet whenever good came they claimed it as their due, and whenever ill struck they took it for an ill omen attending Moses; the Quran corrects them, that the cause of their ill omens is from Allah, though most do not know. Hardening further, they told Moses that whatever sign he brought to bewitch them, they would not believe.

So the signs came in force: a flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood, as distinct signs. The commentators fill in the sequence, that these fell in successive years while Pharaoh, warned by Haman that releasing the Israelites would cost him his throne, kept breaking his word [21]. Whenever a plague fell, his people begged Moses to pray it away and promised to believe and let the Children of Israel go; whenever relief came, they broke the promise. When their appointed term was reached, God took vengeance and drowned them in the sea.

The verses then turn to reward. The people who had been abased were made heirs to the east and west of the blessed land, their Lord's best word fulfilled because they were patient, while all that Pharaoh had built was destroyed. Yet once carried across the water, the Israelites came upon a people cleaving to idols and asked Moses to make them a god of the same kind. Tabatabai reads this as the reflex of a people still bound to the senses, drawn to copy what they saw [2]. Moses answers that they are an ignorant lot: what the idolaters practice is bound to perish and their works come to naught. Shall he seek them a god other than Allah, who has graced them over all the nations? The passage closes by pressing the rescue home: remember your deliverance from Pharaoh's clan, who slaughtered your sons and spared your women, a great test from your Lord.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: العياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام أنه سئل ما الطوفان فقال هو طوفان الماء والطاعون
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: Al-Ayyashi relates that al-Sadiq was asked what the flood was, and he answered: it is the flood of water and the plague.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: العياشي عن الرضا عليه السلام الرّجز هو الثلج ثم قال خراسان بلاد رجز
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Rida

text.en: Al-Ayyashi relates from al-Rida that the plague (rijz) is the snow. Then he said: Khurasan is a land of rijz.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ومثله ما روي عن أبي عبد الله ع أنه أصابهم ثلج أحمر ولم يروه قبل ذلك فماتوا فيه وجزعوا وأصابهم ما لم يعهدوه قبله

text.en: It is narrated from al-Sadiq that a red snow, which they had never seen before, fell upon them; they died in it, panicked, and were struck by what they had not known before.

note.en: On one reading, the 'best word' fulfilled here is God's promise in Surah al-Qasas to favor those who had been abased and make them leaders and heirs [6].
The commentators note this request was unbelief spoken only by the ignorant among Moses' people, not by the righteous believers with him [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: قال علي (عليه السلام) لرأس الجالوت … و أنتم، لم تجف أقدامكم من ماء البحر حتى قلتم لموسى (عليه السلام): { ٱجْعَلْ لَّنَآ إِلَـٰهاً كَمَا لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ }
narrations.chain: Ibn Shahrashub

text.en: Ali said to the Exilarch, who had taunted that the Muslims turned their swords on one another within thirty years of their Prophet: And you, your feet had not dried from the sea before you said to Moses, 'Make for us a god like their gods.'

perspectives.en: On 'so that they may take admonition' (verse 130), the Shia commentator al-Tusi holds the verse disproves the determinists (the Mujbira): God afflicted Pharaoh's people precisely so they would take heed and turn back, which shows He did not will their unbelief [9]. Al-Razi records the same free-will reading from al-Qadi, that God acted intending them to remember and not to persist in disbelief, but relays al-Wahidi's reply that God's 'intending' here only resembles a trial, since real testing is impossible for Him [55]. Both traditions read the words the same way; they part over what those words imply about God's will.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: لهذه العلة لما شاهدوا في مسيرهم قوماً يعكفون على أصنام لهم استحسنوا مثل ذلك لأنفسهم فسألوا موسى عليه السلام أن يجعل لهم إلهاً كما لهم آلهه يعكفون عليها

sources.gloss: For this reason, when on their march they saw a people devoted to their idols, they found the like of it appealing for themselves and asked Moses to make them a god, like the gods those people cleaved to.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ومعناه ولقد عاقبنا قوم فرعون بالجدوب والقحوط { ونقص من الثمرات } أي وأخذناهم مع القحط وإجداب الأرض بنقصان من الثمرات

sources.gloss: Its meaning: We punished Pharaoh's people with droughts and famines; and 'a loss of produce', that is, We seized them, along with the drought and the barren land, with a shortfall of fruits.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ومثله ما روي عن أبي عبد الله ع أنه أصابهم ثلج أحمر ولم يروه قبل ذلك فماتوا فيه

sources.gloss: Similar to it is what is narrated from Abu Abdillah: a red snow, which they had never seen before, fell upon them, and they died in it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل: إن الكلمة الحسنى قولـه سبحانه { ونريد أن نمن على الذين استضعفوا في الأرض } [القصص: 4]

sources.gloss: It is said the 'best word' is His saying, 'And We desire to show favor to those who were abased in the land' (al-Qasas 4).

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهذا كفر ربما قاله الجهال من قومه دون المؤمنين الأخيار

sources.gloss: This is unbelief that perhaps the ignorant among his people said, not the righteous believers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والآية تدل على بطلان مذهب المجبرة من أن الله تعالى يريد الكفر المعاصي، لأنه بين أنه فعل بهم ذلك لكي يذكروا

sources.gloss: The verse proves false the doctrine of the Mujbira (determinists) that God wills unbelief and disobedience, for He made clear that He did this to them so that they might take heed.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فأنزل الله عليهم في تلك السنة الطوفان، فخرب دورهم ومساكنهم حتى خرجوا إلى البرية وضربوا الخيام … فقال له هامان إن خلت عن بني إسرائيل غلبك موسى وأزال ملكك، فقبل منه ولم يخل عن بني إسرائيل … فأنزل الله عليهم في السنة الثانية الجراد … فأنزل الله عليهم في السنة الثالثة القمل

sources.gloss: God sent upon them the flood that year, ruining their homes so that they went out to the open country and pitched tents. Haman said to him: if you release the Children of Israel, Moses will overcome you and take away your kingdom, so he accepted from him and did not release them. In the second year God sent the locusts, and in the third year the lice.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال علي (عليه السلام) لرأس الجالوت … و أنتم، لم تجف أقدامكم من ماء البحر حتى قلتم لموسى (عليه السلام): { ٱجْعَلْ لَّنَآ إِلَـٰهاً كَمَا لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ }

sources.gloss: Ali said to the Exilarch: And you, your feet had not dried from the sea water before you said to Moses, 'Make for us a god like their gods.'

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: العياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام أنه سئل ما الطوفان فقال هو طوفان الماء والطاعون … العياشي عن الرضا عليه السلام الرّجز هو الثلج ثم قال خراسان بلاد رجز

sources.gloss: Al-Ayyashi from al-Sadiq: he was asked what the flood was, and he said it is the flood of water and the plague. Al-Ayyashi from al-Rida: the plague (rijz) is the snow; then he said Khurasan is a land of rijz.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: قال القاضي: هذه الآية تدل على أنه تعالى فعل ذلك إرادة منه أن يتذكروا، لا أن يقيموا على ما هم عليه من الكفر. أجاب الواحدي عنه: بأنه قد جاء لفظ الابتلاء والاختبار في القرآن، لا بمعنى أنه تعالى يمتحنهم، لأن ذلك على الله تعالى محال، بل بمعنى أنه تعالى عاملهم معاملة تشبه الابتلاء والامتحان

sources.gloss: Al-Qadi said: this verse shows that God did that intending them to take heed, not to persist in their unbelief. Al-Wahidi answered him: the words 'trial' and 'testing' occur in the Quran not meaning that God tests them, for that is impossible for God, but meaning that He treated them in a manner resembling a trial.

essay.en: The passage opens on an appointment. God calls Moses to a tryst of thirty nights, completed with ten, so the term is forty, and before leaving Moses sets his brother Aaron over his people, charging him to set things right and not follow the agents of corruption. Tabrisi takes Moses's naming of Aaron, himself a sent prophet, as his deputy to prove that leadership is a station separate from prophethood, not contained within it [2]. At the tryst his Lord speaks to him, and Moses asks to be shown God, that he may look upon Him. The answer is 'You shall not see Me'; God discloses Himself to the mountain, which is levelled, and Moses falls swooning, then wakes as 'the first of the faithful.' Tabrisi's strongest reading is that Moses, knowing his Lord is beyond the senses, asked not for himself but for a people who had demanded to see God openly [3]. God then tells Moses He has chosen him over the people with His messages and His speech, and writes for him in the Tablets advice and detail on all things, bidding him take them with power and his people hold to the best of them [4]. The passage closes on a warning: God will turn the arrogant away from His signs. Tusi rejects reading this as turning them from belief, since God does not command belief and then bar it [10]; they are turned away because they denied the signs, and the works of such deniers come to nothing.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن الله خالف علمه علم الموقتين … أما إن موسى لم يكن يعلم بتلك العشر، و لا بنو إسرائيل، فلما حدثهم. قالوا: كذب موسى، و أخلفنا موسى. فإن حدثتم به فقولوا: صدق الله و رسوله، تؤجروا مرتين
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: God's knowledge differs from the knowledge of those who fix times. Moses did not know of those ten nights, nor did the Children of Israel; when he told them and it ran on they said, 'Moses lied, Moses broke his word.' If you relate this, say, 'God and His Messenger spoke truly,' and be rewarded twice.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إن كليم الله موسى بن عمران (عليه السلام) علم أن الله تعالى عز أن يرى بالأبصار، و لكنه لما كلمه الله عز و جل و قربه نجيا رجع إلى قومه فأخبرهم أن الله عز و جل كلمه و قربه و ناجاه، فقالوا: لن نؤمن لك حتى نسمع كلامه كما سمعت … فقالوا له: لن نؤمن لك بأن الذي سمعناه كلام الله حتى نرى الله جهرة
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Tamim ibn Abdillah al-Qurashi, from his father, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Jahm

text.en: Moses knew that God is too exalted to be seen by eyes. But when God spoke to him and drew him near in intimacy, he returned to his people and told them God had spoken to him. They said, 'We will not believe you until we hear His speech as you did' … then, 'until we see God openly.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنا أوّل من آمن وصدق بأنّك لا ترى

text.en: I am the first to believe and to affirm that You cannot be seen.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا موسى تدري لما اصطفيتك بكلامي دون خلقي … اني قلبت عبادي ظهراً لبطن فلم أجد فيهم أحداً أذلّ لي نفساً منك يا موسى إنّك إذاً صليت وضعت خدّك على التراب

text.en: God revealed to Moses: 'O Moses, do you know why I chose you with My speech above My creation?' Moses said, 'Lord, why?' He revealed: 'O Moses, I turned My servants over, front to back, and found none more lowly before Me than you; when you pray you lay your cheek upon the dust.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ما بعث الله نبياً إلا أعطاه من العلم بعضه ما خلا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فإنه أعطاه من العلم كله … فهي الزيادة التي عندنا من العلم الذي لم يكن عند أحدٍ من الأوصياء والأنبياء ولا ذرية الأنبياء غيرنا
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Attab, from Abu Ja'far, from his father

text.en: God sent no prophet without giving him part of the knowledge, save the Prophet, to whom He gave all of it. That is the surplus of knowledge with us, held by none of the executors, prophets, or prophets' progeny but us.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما أنزل الألواح على موسى (عليه السلام) أنزلها عليه و فيها تبيان كل شيء، كان أو هو كائن إلى أن تقوم الساعة … و الألواح عندنا، و عصا موسى عندنا، و نحن ورثنا النبيين
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When God sent down the Tablets to Moses, He sent them with the exposition of everything, whatever was or will be until the Hour rises. The Tablets are with us, the staff of Moses is with us, and we are the heirs of the prophets.

perspectives.en: On 'You shall not see Me,' the two traditions divide. Tabrisi gives as the strongest view that Moses, knowing his Lord is not grasped by the senses, asked to see God only for his people who had demanded it, since a vision that would imply a body is impossible [3]. Ibn Kathir holds instead that 'shall not' denies the vision only in this world, for mass-transmitted reports affirm that the believers will see God in the Hereafter [34]. Qurtubi states the split plainly: for Ahl al-Sunna vision is permissible, while for their opponents Moses asked for the people's sake, to show them it is not [38].

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي هذا دلالة على أن منزلة الإمامة منفصلة من النبوة وغير داخلة فيها

sources.gloss: In this is a proof that the station of leadership is separate from prophethood and not contained within it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أنه لم يسأل الرؤية لنفسه وإنما سألها لقومه

sources.gloss: He did not ask to see for himself but asked it for his people.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { وأمر قومك يأخذوا بأحسنها } أي بما فيها من أحسن المحاسن وهي الفرائض والنوافل

sources.gloss: 'Bid your people to hold to the best of them' means the finest of what is in them: the obligatory and recommended acts.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومن زعم انه بمعنى سأصرف عن الايمان بآياتي فقد أخطأ، لانه تعالى لا يأمر بالايمان ثم يمنع منه

sources.gloss: Whoever claims it means 'I will turn them from believing in My signs' has erred, for God does not command belief and then prevent it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أما إن موسى لم يكن يعلم بتلك العشر، و لا بنو إسرائيل، فلما حدثهم. قالوا: كذب موسى، و أخلفنا موسى

sources.gloss: Moses did not know of those ten nights, nor did the Children of Israel; when he told them they said, 'Moses lied, Moses broke his word with us.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن كليم الله موسى بن عمران (عليه السلام) علم أن الله تعالى عز أن يرى بالأبصار

sources.gloss: God's interlocutor Moses son of Imran knew that God is too exalted to be seen by the eyes.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أنزلها عليه و فيها تبيان كل شيء، كان أو هو كائن إلى أن تقوم الساعة

sources.gloss: He sent them down containing the exposition of everything, whatever was or will be until the Hour rises.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أنا أوّل من آمن وصدق بأنّك لا ترى

sources.gloss: I am the first to believe and to affirm that You cannot be seen.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: اني قلبت عبادي ظهراً لبطن فلم أجد فيهم أحداً أذلّ لي نفساً منك

sources.gloss: I turned My servants over, front to back, and found none more lowly before Me than you.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: ما بعث الله نبياً إلا أعطاه من العلم بعضه ما خلا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فإنه أعطاه من العلم كله

sources.gloss: God sent no prophet without giving him part of the knowledge, except the Prophet, to whom He gave all of it.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: فاستدل به المعتزلة على نفي الرؤية في الدنيا والآخرة، وهذا أضعف الأقوال لأنه قد تواترت الأحاديث عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن المؤمنين يرون الله في الدار الآخرة

sources.gloss: The Mu'tazila used it to deny the vision in this world and the next; this is the weakest view, for mass-transmitted reports affirm the believers will see God in the Hereafter.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: عند أهل السنة والجماعة الرؤيةُ جائزةٌ. وعند المبتدعة سأل لأجل القوم ليبيّن لهم أنها غير جائزة

sources.gloss: With Ahl al-Sunna wa'l-Jama'a the vision is permissible; with the innovators, he asked for the people's sake, to show them it is not permissible.

essay.en:
In Moses' absence his people take a calf cast from their ornaments, a lifeless body that gives out a lowing sound. Al-Mizan explains that they were a sense-bound, material people, which is why they had craved a tangible god they could see [1]. Commentators differ over how the calf could low: al-Hasan says al-Samiri cast into it dust from the hoofprint of Gabriel's horse so that it turned to flesh, while al-Jubba'i and al-Balkhi say he contrived the sound with air [5]. The Quran rebukes them: it neither spoke to them nor guided them to any way, yet they took it up.

When remorse overtakes them and they see they have gone astray, they confess they are lost unless their Lord forgives them. Al-Tibyan notes that they now knew their straying and saw the falseness of what they had done [6]. Moses returns angry and grieving, throws down the tablets, and seizes his brother's head. Aaron pleads that the people had overpowered him and nearly killed him. Al-Tibyan explains that Aaron spoke so lest the ignorant among them think Moses had struck him in contempt, and that Moses gripped his head as a man grips himself in distress, not in anger [7]. Then Moses prays that God forgive him and his brother and admit them into His mercy. Al-Tibyan reads this prayer not as repentance from any sin but as Moses turning wholly to God, for the prophets commit nothing ugly, neither great nor small [8].

note.en: Though the verse blames the whole people, commentators say it was al-Samiri, feared and obeyed among them, who cast the calf from the ornaments left in their hands after Pharaoh drowned [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أن في ما ناجى موسى ربه أن قال يا رب هذا السامري صنع العجل فالخوار من صنعه قال فأوحى الله إليه يا موسى إنّ تلك فتنتي فلا تفحص عنها
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Baqir

text.en: In Moses' whispered prayer to his Lord he said, 'My Lord, this al-Samiri made the calf, so from where is its lowing?' God revealed to him, 'O Moses, that is My trial, so do not probe into it.'

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: قوله تعالى: { وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فِيۤ أَيْدِيهِمْ } يعني لما جاءهم موسى و أحرق العجل { قَالُواْ لَئِن لَّمْ يَرْحَمْنَا رَبُّنَا وَيَغْفِرْ لَنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْخَاسِرِينَ }

text.en: His words 'when they became remorseful' mean: when Moses came to them and burned the calf, they said, 'Should our Lord have no mercy on us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله تبارك و تعالى لما أخبر موسى أن قومه اتخذوا عجلا له خوار، فلم يقع منه موقع العيان، فلما رآهم اشتد غضبه فألقى الألواح من يده … و للرؤية فضل على الخبر
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When God informed Moses that his people had taken a lowing calf, it did not strike him as the sight of it did; when he saw them his anger intensified and he threw the tablets from his hand. And Abu Abdillah said: seeing has an advantage over report.

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Mu'minin
narrations.arabic: ولي بأخي هارون أسوة إذ قال لأخيه: { ٱبْنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱسْتَضْعَفُونِي وَكَادُواْ يَقْتُلُونَنِي } فإن قلتم لم يستضعفوه و لم يشرفوا على قتله فقد كفرتم، و إن قلتم استضعفوه و أشرفوا على قتله، فلذلك سكت عنهم، فالوصي أعذر
narrations.chain: Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Alawi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from al-Fadl ibn Khabbab al-Jumahi, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Himsi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Ta'i, from his father, from Ibn Mas'ud

text.en: I have a model in my brother Aaron, when he said to his brother, 'Son of my mother, the people thought me weak and were about to kill me.' If you claim they did not, you have disbelieved; if they did, that is why he stayed silent - so the successor is the more excused.

perspectives.en: On why Moses prays 'forgive me and my brother,' the traditions diverge. Al-Tibyan insists the prayer is no repentance from sin, since the prophets commit nothing ugly, great or small [8]. Tabari reads it as Moses seeking pardon for his rough handling of his brother and for something earlier between Aaron and God [18]. Ibn Kathir has Moses seize Aaron's head fearing he had fallen short in restraining the people, then pray once he was certain of Aaron's innocence [20]. The Shia reading keeps both brothers free of fault throughout.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: كانوا قوماً ماديين حسيين يجرون في حياتهم على أصالة الحس

sources.gloss: They were a material, sense-bound people who lived by the primacy of the senses.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: يعني السامري ومن جرى على طريقته … وكان السامري عندهم مهيباً مطاعاً فيما بينهم

sources.gloss: Meaning al-Samiri and those who followed his way … al-Samiri was held in awe and obeyed among them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فقال الحسن: قبض السامري قبضة من تراب من أثر فرس جبرائيل (ع) يوم قطع البحر فقذف ذلك التراب في فم العجل، فتحول لحماً ودماً … وقال الجبائي والبلخي: إِنما احتال بادخال الريح فيه حتى سمع له كالخوار

sources.gloss: al-Hasan said: al-Samiri took a handful of dust from the track of Gabriel's horse on the day the sea parted and cast it into the calf's mouth, and it turned to flesh and blood … al-Jubba'i and al-Balkhi said: he contrived it by letting air into it so a lowing was heard.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: علموا { أنهم قد ضلوا } وتبينوا بطلان ما كانوا عليه من عبادة العجل

sources.gloss: They knew that they had gone astray and saw clearly the falseness of the calf-worship they had been on.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: حكاية عما قال هارون لموسى حين أخذ برأسه خوفاً من أن يدخل الشبهة على جهال قومه … فأجرى موسى هارون مجرى نفسه

sources.gloss: A report of what Aaron said to Moses when he took his head, fearing that doubt would enter the ignorant among his people … Moses treated Aaron as he would treat himself.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وكان هذا الدعاء من موسى انقطاعاً منه الى الله تعالى، وتقرباً اليه لا أنه كان وقع منه أو من أخيه قبيح … أن الانبياء (ع) لا يجوز عليهم شيء من القبائح لا كبيرها ولا صغيرها

sources.gloss: This prayer was Moses turning wholly to God and drawing near to Him, not that anything ugly had occurred from him or his brother … the prophets can commit nothing ugly, neither its great nor its small.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فلما رآهم اشتد غضبه فألقى الألواح من يده

sources.gloss: When he saw them his anger intensified and he threw the tablets from his hand.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ولي بأخي هارون أسوة إذ قال لأخيه … فالوصي أعذر

sources.gloss: I have a model in my brother Aaron when he said to his brother … so the successor is the more excused.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: يا موسى إنّ تلك فتنتي فلا تفحص عنها

sources.gloss: O Moses, that is My trial, so do not probe into it.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: مستغفرا من فعله بأخيه، ولأخيه من سالف له بـينه وبـين الله

sources.gloss: Seeking forgiveness for his act toward his brother, and for his brother from something prior between him and God.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ } خوفاً أن يكون قد قصر في نهيهم … فلما تحقق موسى عليه السلام براءة ساحة هارون

sources.gloss: He seized his brother's head, fearing Aaron had fallen short in forbidding them … then Moses became certain of Aaron's innocence.

title.en: Wrath, mercy, and the untaught prophet

essay.en: The passage closes the story of the golden calf and opens the way back from it. Those who took the calf for worship are warned that their Lord's wrath and abasement will overtake them in the life of the world, and that this is how God requites every fabricator; on one report their abasement is the command that they put themselves to death [3]. Yet the door stays open: whoever commits misdeeds, then repents and believes, finds his Lord all-forgiving, all-merciful [8]. When Moses' anger subsides he picks up the tablets he had thrown down, whose inscriptions hold guidance and mercy - and Tusi notes that casting the Torah in anger and then recovering it for the wisdom in it is no turning away from it [9]. Moses then chooses seventy men for the tryst, and an earthquake seizes them. Al-Mizan reads it as the thunderbolt of 2:55 and 4:153: they had demanded to see God, were struck dead, then revived [2]; Tusi adds that these seventy were neither infallible nor prophets [10]. Moses pleads for pardon, and God answers that His mercy embraces all things but will be inscribed for the Godwary. That mercy, Tabrisi records, was claimed in turn by Iblis and by the People of the Book before it settled on this community [5] - the community of the untaught prophet whom they find written in the Torah and the Gospel, who lifts from them the burdens and shackles that had bound them [15].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قلت: يا أخا أسلم من تعرف منهم قال: أعرف خيرهم و سيدهم و أفضلهم هارون بن سعد، قال: قلت: يا أخا أسلم رأس العجلية، أما سمعت الله عز و جل يقول: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ سَيَنالُهُمْ غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَ ذِلَّةٌ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Masud, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: A man told me the best and chief of the Zaydiyya was Harun ibn Sad. I said: brother of Aslam, that is the head of the calf-party. Have you not heard God say, 'Indeed those who took up the calf shall be overtaken by their Lord's wrath and abasement in the life of the world'?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: مَا أَخْلَصَ الْعَبْدُ الإيمَانَ بِالله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْماً … إِلا زَهَّدَهُ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَبَصَّرَهُ دَاءَهَا وَدَوَاءَهَا فَأَثْبَتَ الْحِكْمَةَ فِي قَلْبِهِ وَأَنْطَقَ بِهَا لِسَانَهُ ثُمَّ تَلا إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ سَيَنالُهُمْ غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَذِلَّةٌ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُفْتَرِينَ فَلا تَرَى صَاحِبَ بِدْعَةٍ إِلا ذَلِيلاً
narrations.chain: Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from al-Sindi, from Abu Jafar

text.en: No servant keeps his faith in God sincere for forty days but God makes him renounce the world, shows him its disease and cure, sets wisdom in his heart and makes his tongue speak it. So you will not see a man of innovation, who fabricates against God, His Messenger and his household, but abased.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن موسى اختار سبعين رجلا من قومه، فلما أخذتهم الرجفة قال: رب أصحابي أصحابي. قال: إني أبدلك بهم من هو خير لكم منهم. فقال: إني عرفتهم و وجدت ريحهم، قال: فبعثهم الله له أنبياء
narrations.chain: al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Moses chose seventy men from his people, and when the earthquake seized them he cried, 'My Lord, my companions, my companions!' He said: I shall replace them with ones better for you than them. Moses said: I knew them and found their scent. So God raised them up for him as prophets.

narrations.speaker: al-Qaim
narrations.arabic: هذا موسى كليم الله مع وفور عقله و كمال علمه و نزول الوحي عليه اختار من أعيان قومه و وجوه عسكره لميقات ربه سبعين رجلا، ممن لا يشك في إيمانهم و إخلاصهم، فوقعت خيرته على المنافقين
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, by his chain, from Sad ibn Abdullah al-Qummi, from al-Qaim

text.en: This is Moses, who spoke with God, with his full reason, perfect knowledge, and revelation upon him. He chose seventy of the notables of his people for his Lord's tryst, men whose faith and sincerity he did not doubt, yet his choice fell upon the hypocrites.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: النور في هذا الموضع أمير المؤمنين و الأئمة (عليهم السلام)
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, by his chain from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The light in this place is Amir al-Mu'minin and the Imams.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Jawad
narrations.arabic: قيل يزعمون أنّه انّما سمي الأمّي لأنه لم يحسن أن يكتب فقال كذبوا عليهم لعنة الله انّى ذلك والله يقول هو الذي بعثني في الأُمّيين رسولاً منهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة فكيف كان يعلمهم ما لا يحسن … وانّما سمِّي الأُمّي لأنّه كان من أهل مكة ومكة من أمّهات القرى

text.en: He was asked why the Prophet is called 'ummi.' People claim it is because he could not write. He said: they lie. God says He raised among the ummiyyin a messenger who teaches them the Book and wisdom; how could he teach what he did not know? He was called ummi only because he was of Mecca, a mother-town.

perspectives.en: Both traditions read verse 157 as the Torah and the Gospel foretelling Muhammad, whom the People of the Book find described in their own scriptures. They part over 'the light that has been sent down with him.' Shia narrations gloss this light as Amir al-Mu'minin and the Imams, so that following the Prophet reaches to following his appointed successors [18]. Qurtubi and the Sunni commentators instead take the felicitous to be simply those who follow the Prophet in the religion and law he brought, reading no such designation into the light [35].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فأخذتهم الصاعقة فماتوا ثم أحياهم الله بدعوة موسى

sources.gloss: The thunderbolt seized them and they died, then God revived them at Moses' prayer.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال الزجاج: والذلة ما أمروا به من قتل أنفسهم

sources.gloss: Zajjaj said: the abasement is what they were commanded - to put themselves to death.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال إبليس: أنا من ذلك الشيء فنزعها الله من إبليس بقولـه فسأكتبها للذين يتقون إلى آخر الآية فقال اليهود والنصارى: نحن نتَّقي ونؤتي الزكاة ونؤمن بآيات ربنا فنزعها منهم وجعلها لهذه الأمة

sources.gloss: Iblis said: I am among that 'thing' - so God removed it from him with 'I shall appoint it for those who are Godwary.' Then the Jews and Christians said: we are Godwary, give zakat and believe in our Lord's signs - so He removed it from them and gave it to this community.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: من بعدها يعني من بعد السيئة لغفور رحيم يعني يغفرها لهم ويسترها عليهم، لرحمته بعباده

sources.gloss: 'after it' means after the misdeed; 'all-forgiving, all-merciful' means He forgives them and veils it for them, out of His mercy to His servants.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على أنه يجوز إِلقاء التوراة للغضب الذي يظهر بالقائها ثم أخذها، للحكمة التي فيها من غير أن يكون إِلقاؤها رغبة عنها

sources.gloss: The verse shows it is permissible to cast down the Torah for the anger its casting displays, then take it up again for the wisdom in it, without the casting being a turning away from it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ولم يثبت أن السبعين كانوا معصومين، ولا أنهم كانوا أنبياء

sources.gloss: It is not established that the seventy were infallible, nor that they were prophets.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: الثقل الذي كان على بني إسرائيل … فرفع ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله عن أمته

sources.gloss: The burden that lay on the Children of Israel... which the Messenger lifted from his community.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن موسى اختار سبعين رجلا من قومه، فلما أخذتهم الرجفة قال: رب أصحابي أصحابي. قال: إني أبدلك بهم من هو خير لكم منهم

sources.gloss: Moses chose seventy men from his people; when the earthquake seized them he said: My Lord, my companions, my companions! He said: I shall replace them with ones better for you.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: النور في هذا الموضع أمير المؤمنين و الأئمة
