sources.gloss: The light in this place is Amir al-Mu'minin and the Imams.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وانّما سمِّي الأُمّي لأنّه كان من أهل مكة ومكة من أمّهات القرى

sources.gloss: He was called 'ummi' only because he was from the people of Mecca, and Mecca is one of the mother-towns.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: و «يَتَّبِعُونَ» يعني في شرعه ودينه وما جاء به

sources.gloss: 'those who follow' means in his law, his religion, and what he brought.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: مَا أَخْلَصَ الْعَبْدُ الإيمَانَ بِالله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْماً … فَلا تَرَى صَاحِبَ بِدْعَةٍ إِلا ذَلِيلاً

sources.gloss: No servant keeps his faith in God sincere for forty days... so you will not see a man of innovation except abased.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad asif al-muhsini

excerpt.text: يا أخا أسلم رأس العجلية، أما سمعت الله عز و جل يقول: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ سَيَنالُهُمْ غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَ ذِلَّةٌ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا

sources.gloss: Brother of Aslam, that is the head of the calf-party! Have you not heard God say: Indeed those who took up the calf shall be overtaken by their Lord's wrath and abasement in the life of the world?

essay.en:
The passage opens with a command to the Prophet: proclaim to all mankind, Arab and non-Arab alike, that he is God's messenger to every one of them [3]. The One who sends him owns the heavens and the earth; there is no god but Him, and He alone gives life and death [3][6]. So people are to believe in Allah and in the untaught prophet, who himself believes in Allah and His words, and to follow him to be guided [3]. He is called ummi because he belongs to Mecca, the mother of towns, not because he could not read [15].

The passage then turns to the people of Moses, among whom is a nation who guide by the truth and judge justly. Commentators differ over who they are; some name a people settled beyond China who never altered their faith, a reading traced to al-Baqir [4][7]. God split Bani Israil into twelve tribes; when they asked for water, Moses struck the rock and twelve springs gushed out, each tribe knowing its drinking place, while clouds shaded them and manna and quails came down. They wronged only themselves.

They were told to settle a town in the holy land [2], to eat freely, to say hittah as a plea for their sins to be lifted [9], and to enter its gate prostrate. But the wrongdoers among them changed the word they had been given, and a plague was sent down from the sky [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Hasan
narrations.arabic: جاء نفر من اليهود إلى رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) فقالوا: يا محمد، أنت الذي تزعم أنك رسول الله … قالوا: إلى من، إلى العرب أم إلى العجم، أم إلينا؟ فأنزل الله عز و جل: { قُلْ يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعاً }
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from al-Hasan ibn Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib

text.en: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah and said, 'Muhammad, you claim to be the messenger of Allah.' They asked, 'To whom - the Arabs, the non-Arabs, or us?' Then Allah revealed, 'Say, O mankind! I am the Apostle of Allah to you all.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في قول الله: { وَمِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ } ، قال: قوم موسى هم أهل الإسلام
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Concerning God's words, 'Among the people of Moses is a nation who guide by the truth and do justice thereby,' he said: The people of Moses are the people of Islam.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إذا قام قائم آل محمد (صلى الله عليه و آله) استخرج من ظهر الكوفة سبعة و عشرين رجلا، خمسة عشر من قوم موسى الذين يقضون بالحق و به يعدلون، و سبعة من أصحاب الكهف، و يوشع وصي موسى، و مؤمن آل فرعون، و سلمان الفارسي، و أبا دجانة الأنصاري، و مالك الأشتر
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When the Qa'im of the Family of Muhammad rises, he will bring out from the outskirts of Kufa twenty-seven men: fifteen from the people of Moses who judge by the truth and do justice thereby, seven of the People of the Cave, Joshua the executor of Moses, the believer of Pharaoh's house, Salman, Abu Dujana, and Malik al-Ashtar.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Abi Talib
narrations.arabic: على كم افترقت بنو إسرائيل بعد موسى؟ … كذبت و الله الذي لا إله إلا هو، لقد افترقت على إحدى و سبعين فرقة، كلها في النار إلا واحدة، فإن الله يقول: { وَمِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ } فهذه التي تنجو
narrations.chain: from Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri, who heard Ali ibn Abi Talib

text.en: Ali asked the exilarch: Into how many groups did Bani Israil split after Moses? He said, 'One.' Ali said, 'You have lied, by Allah. They split into seventy-one sects, all in the Fire but one; for Allah says, "Among the people of Moses is a nation who guide by the truth" - this is the one that is saved.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن القائم إذا قام بمكة و أراد أن يتوجه إلى الكوفة نادى مناديه: ألا لا يحمل أحد منكم طعاما و لا شرابا. و يحمل حجر موسى بن عمران (عليه السلام) و هو وقر بعير، فلا ينزل منزلا إلا انبعثت عين منه، فمن كان جائعا شبع، و من كان ظامئا روي، فهو زادهم حتى ينزلوا النجف من ظهر الكوفة
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Sa'id al-Khurasani, from Abu Abdillah, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: When the Qa'im rises at Mecca and sets out for Kufa, his herald calls, 'Let none of you carry food or drink.' He carries the stone of Moses ibn Imran, a camel's load; at no halt does he stop but a spring bursts from it, feeding the hungry and quenching the thirsty, until they reach Najaf behind Kufa.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ألواح موسى (عليه السلام) عندنا، و عصا موسى عندنا، و نحن ورثة النبيين
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Imran ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The tablets of Moses are with us, and the staff of Moses is with us, and we are the heirs of the prophets.

perspectives.en: Both traditions ask who the 'nation who guide by the truth' among Moses's people are. Al-Razi lists several Sunni answers: Jews of the Prophet's time who embraced Islam, like Abdullah ibn Salam; those who kept Moses's true religion before it was altered; and a people who emerged beyond China, still facing the qibla and keeping the faith [29]. Shia commentators report the same people beyond China on al-Baqir's authority, but press the verse further: no age lacks guides by the truth, God's infallible proofs over creation [7], and fifteen of Moses's people will return with the Qa'im [13].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: القرية هي التي كانت في الأرض المقدسة أُمروا بدخولها وقتال أهلها من العمالقة وإخراجهم منها فتمرّدوا عن الأمر، وردّوا على موسى عليه السلام فابتلوا بالتيه، والقصة مذكورة في سورة المائدة.

sources.gloss: The town was in the holy land; they were ordered to enter it, fight its Amalekite people and drive them out, but they rebelled against the command and rejected Moses, so they were afflicted with wandering; the story is in Surah al-Ma'idah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { يحيي } الأَموات { ويميت } الأَحياء لا يقدر أحد على الإِحياء والإِماتة سواه

sources.gloss: 'He gives life' to the dead 'and brings death' to the living; none but Him has power to give life or bring death.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أنهم قوم من وراء الصين وبينهم وبين الصين وادٍ جار من الرمل لم يغيروا ولم يبدلوا عن ابن عباس والسدي والربيع والضحاك وعطاء وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع

sources.gloss: They are a people beyond China, between whom and China lies a flowing valley of sand; they neither changed nor altered - from Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, al-Rabi, al-Dahhak and Ata, and it is related from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وإنما وصفه بأنه يحيي ويميت لأنه لا يقدر على الاحياء إلا الله، ولاعلى الاماتة أيضاً سواه

sources.gloss: He described Himself as giving life and death because none but Allah has power to give life, nor any but Him to bring death.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: عندنا في كل عصر لا يخلون من قوم بهذا الوصف وهم حجج الله على خلقه، المعصومين الذين لا يجوز عليهم الخطأ والزلل

sources.gloss: In our view, no age is without a people of this description; they are God's proofs over His creation, the infallible ones who are not liable to error or slip.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله { وقولوا حطة } معناه قولوا حط عنا ذنوبنا وهو بمنزلة الاستغفار والتوبة

sources.gloss: His words 'and say hittah' mean: say, 'Lift our sins from us' - it stands in the place of seeking forgiveness and repentance.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ارسل عليهم عند ذلك رجزاً وهو العذاب والعقوبة

sources.gloss: He sent upon them a rijz - that is, punishment and chastisement.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قالوا: إلى من، إلى العرب أم إلى العجم، أم إلينا؟

sources.gloss: They said: To whom - the Arabs, the non-Arabs, or us?

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: خمسة عشر من قوم موسى الذين يقضون بالحق و به يعدلون

sources.gloss: Fifteen from the people of Moses who judge by the truth and do justice thereby.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ألواح موسى (عليه السلام) عندنا، و عصا موسى عندنا، و نحن ورثة النبيين

sources.gloss: The tablets of Moses are with us, and the staff of Moses is with us, and we are the heirs of the prophets.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: انّما سمِّي الأُمّي لأنّه كان من أهل مكة ومكة من أمّهات القرى

sources.gloss: He was called ummi only because he was from the people of Mecca, and Mecca is one of the mother-towns.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: فقيل هم اليهود الذين كانوا في زمان الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام، وأسلموا مثل عبد الله بن سلام

sources.gloss: It is said they are the Jews who lived in the Messenger's time and embraced Islam, like Abdullah ibn Salam.

title.en: The town that broke the Sabbath

essay.en:
The passage turns to the Children of Israel and a coastal town that broke the Sabbath. God tells the Prophet to 'Ask them about the town that was situated on the seaside,' where fish surfaced openly on the Sabbath, when fishing was forbidden, and vanished on other days - a test. Tusi reads 'ask them' as a question of rebuke, not of seeking information [7], and the commentators differ over the town's name, calling it Ayla, Madyan, or Tiberias [2].

When one group asked, 'Why do you advise a people whom Allah will destroy,' the warners answered, 'As an excuse before your Lord, and that they may be Godwary.' Tabatabai reads the challengers as themselves God-fearing, who kept clear of the sin but had given up forbidding it [1]. Tusi draws from the warners' reply that forbidding wrong stays obligatory even when the wrongdoer will not be deterred [8].

So when they forgot the reminder, God saved those who forbade evil and seized the wrongdoers, and when they defied the command, told them, 'Be you spurned apes.' The narrations distinguish three groups among the townsfolk [59].

God then proclaimed He would keep sending, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would inflict a terrible punishment on them: the commentators and Abu Ja'far read this as the community of Muhammad taking the jizya, so that the Jews would hold no state [4]. He scattered them into communities, some righteous and some not, and tested them with ease and hardship. An evil posterity then inherited the Book, grabbing the world's cheap gains and saying, 'It will be forgiven us' - taking bribes in judgment [5], against the covenant that they attribute nothing to God but the truth. The passage closes as God holds the mountain above them, as if it were a canopy: Tusi explains it was lifted because they had refused the Torah's heavy rulings, until they submitted and held fast to what they were given [15].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وجدنا في كتاب علي (عليه السلام) أن قوما من أهل أيلة، من قوم ثمود، و أن الحيتان كانت سبقت إليهم يوم السبت ليختبر الله طاعتهم في ذلك، فشرعت إليهم يوم سبتهم في ناديهم، و قدام أبوابهم … ثم إن الشيطان أوحى إلى طائفة منهم: إنما نهيتم عن أكلها يوم السبت و لم تنهوا عن صيدها
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riab, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: We found in the book of Ali that a people of Ayla, of the folk of Thamud, had the fish come to them on the Sabbath to test their obedience, appearing openly in their assembly and at their doors. Then Satan whispered to a group: you were forbidden only to eat them on the Sabbath, not to catch them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: كانوا ثلاثة أصناف: صنف ائتمروا وأمروا [فنجوا] وصنف ائتمروا ولم يأمروا [فمسخوا ذرا] وصنف لم يأتمروا ولم يأمروا فهلكوا
narrations.chain: his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Talha al-Shami, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: They were three groups: a group that restrained themselves and commanded others were saved; a group that restrained themselves but did not command others were metamorphosed into particles; and a group that neither restrained themselves nor commanded others perished.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله خص عباده بآيتين من كتابه أن لا يقولوا حتى يعلموا، و لا يردوا ما لم يعلموا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Yaqub Ishaq ibn Abd Allah, from Abu Abd Allah

text.en: God singled out His servants with two verses of His Book: that they not speak until they know, and that they not reject what they do not know. God said, 'Was not the covenant of the Book taken with them that they shall not attribute anything to Allah except the truth?'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الذين يمسكون بالكتاب … نزلت في آل محمد وأشياعهم
narrations.chain: Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Concerning 'those who hold fast to the Book,' it was revealed about the family of Muhammad and their followers.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما أنزل الله التوراة على بني إسرائيل لم يقبلوه فرفع الله عليهم جبل طور سيناء، فقال لهم موسى عليه السلام إن لم تقبلوه وقع عليكم الجبل، فقبلوه وطأطؤا رؤوسهم

text.en: When God sent down the Torah to the Children of Israel, they would not accept it, so God raised Mount Sinai over them. Musa told them: if you do not accept it, the mountain will fall on you. So they accepted it and bowed their heads.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: العياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام أنّه سئل عن هذه الآية أقوّة في الأبدان أم قوّة في القلوب قال فيهما جميعاً
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: Al-Sadiq was asked about this verse - is the power in the bodies or power in the hearts? He said: in both together.

perspectives.en: On verse 170, 'those who hold fast to the Book,' the Shia narration reads it of the family of Muhammad and their followers [19]. Sunni commentators take it plainly: al-Qurtubi glosses 'the Book' as the Torah, meaning those who act on it [46]. The two traditions also weigh the offenders' neighbours differently. Shia reports say a group who abstained from the sin yet did not forbid it were metamorphosed into particles [59], while Ibn Kathir records that the two groups who spoke up were saved and only the wrongdoers destroyed [36].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وظاهر كلامهم { لم تعظون قوماً الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذاباً شديداً } أنهم كانوا أهل تقوى يجتنبون مخالفة الأمر إلا أنهم تركوا نهيهم عن المنكر

sources.gloss: The plain sense of their words, 'Why do you advise a people whom Allah will destroy,' is that they were people of Godwariness who avoided disobeying the command, except that they had given up forbidding the wrong.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهي إيلة عن ابن عباس. وقيل: هي مدين عنه أيضاً. وقيل: طبرية عن الزهري

sources.gloss: It is Ayla, according to Ibn Abbas; it is also said to be Madyan, on his authority too; and it is said to be Tiberias, on the authority of al-Zuhri.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وأخذ الجزية منهم والمعني به أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عند جميع المفسرين وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر ع وهذا يدل على أن اليهود لا تكون لهم دولة إلى يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: And taking the jizya from them; it means the community of Muhammad, according to all the exegetes, and it is what is reported from Abu Ja'far; this shows the Jews will have no state until the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل: إنهم كانوا يرتشون ويحكمون بجور

sources.gloss: It is said they used to take bribes and judge unjustly.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: سؤال تقرير وتوبيخ لا سؤال استفهام

sources.gloss: A question of affirmation and rebuke, not a question of seeking information.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يجب النهي عن القبيح وإن علم الناهي ان المنهي لا ينزجر ولا يقبل

sources.gloss: Forbidding the wrong is obligatory even when the one forbidding knows the wrongdoer will not be deterred and will not accept.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وكان سبب رفع الجبل عليهم ان موسى عليه السلام لما اتاهم بالتوراة ووقفوا على ما فيها من الاحكام والحدود والتشديد في العبادة ابوا أن يقبلوا ذلك

sources.gloss: The reason the mountain was raised over them was that when Musa brought them the Torah and they saw its rulings, its limits, and the severity of worship in it, they refused to accept it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله الذين يمسكون بالكتاب قال نزلت في آل محمد وأشياعهم

sources.gloss: In the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far, concerning 'those who hold fast to the Book': it was revealed about the family of Muhammad and their followers.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال الصادق عليه السلام: لما أنزل الله التوراة على بني إسرائيل لم يقبلوه فرفع الله عليهم جبل طور سيناء

sources.gloss: Al-Sadiq said: when God sent down the Torah to the Children of Israel, they would not accept it, so God raised Mount Sinai over them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: وجدنا في كتاب علي (عليه السلام) أن قوما من أهل أيلة، من قوم ثمود، و أن الحيتان كانت سبقت إليهم يوم السبت ليختبر الله طاعتهم في ذلك

sources.gloss: We found in the book of Ali that a people of Ayla, of the folk of Thamud, had the fish come to them on the Sabbath so that God might test their obedience.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله خص عباده بآيتين من كتابه أن لا يقولوا حتى يعلموا، و لا يردوا ما لم يعلموا

sources.gloss: God singled out His servants with two verses of His Book: that they not speak until they know, and not reject what they do not know.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: العياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام أنّه سئل عن هذه الآية أقوّة في الأبدان أم قوّة في القلوب قال فيهما جميعاً

sources.gloss: Al-Ayyashi, from al-Sadiq: he was asked about this verse - is the power in the bodies or in the hearts? He said: in both together.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: فلما وقع عليهم غضب الله، نجت الطائفتان اللتان قالوا لم تعظون قوماً الله مهلكهم؟ والذين قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم

sources.gloss: When God's wrath fell upon them, the two groups that had said 'Why do you advise a people whom Allah will destroy' were saved, and those who said 'as an excuse before your Lord'.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: أي بالتوراة، أي بالعمل بها

sources.gloss: That is, the Torah - that is, by acting on it.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: كانوا ثلاثة أصناف: صنف ائتمروا وأمروا [فنجوا] وصنف ائتمروا ولم يأمروا [فمسخوا ذرا] وصنف لم يأتمروا ولم يأمروا فهلكوا

sources.gloss: They were three groups: those who restrained themselves and commanded others - saved; those who restrained themselves but did not command - metamorphosed into particles; and those who neither restrained themselves nor commanded - destroyed.

essay.en:
'When your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants,' the passage opens on a covenant older than the world. God draws every descendant out, makes each a witness over itself, and asks, 'Am I not your Lord?' They answer, 'Yes indeed! We bear witness,' so that no one may plead on the Day of Resurrection that he was unaware, or lay the blame on the idolatry of his fathers. Tabatabai reads the taking as God setting each soul apart as an independent self and then showing it its own reality, so that its 'Yes' is knowledge it will carry [1]. Tabrisi records the accounts scholars gave of the event, and the objection of the verifiers that the wording is 'the Children of Adam' and 'their loins,' not 'Adam' and 'his loin' [4]. God elaborates these signs, Tusi adds, so that people may turn back from disobedience to obedience [8].

A warning follows. 'Relate to them an account of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he cast them off.' Tabatabai takes the signs as inner graces that had lit the path to God for the man, and observes that the commentators differ over who he was [2]. Tabrisi names him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud, as Bal'am ibn Ba'ura, while others name the poet Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt [5]. Tusi reports al-Baqir's ruling that the origin was Bal'am, but that the verse became a parable for everyone who prefers his desire over God's guidance, and he rejects the claim that the signs were prophethood [9]. Had God wished He would have raised him by them; instead he clung to the earth, and his likeness is the dog that lolls out its tongue whether driven off or left alone [10].

The close draws the threads together. Many jinn and humans are winnowed out for hell, created to worship, Tabrisi explains, yet bound for the fire by their own choice, since the lam is one of outcome [6]. Guidance and misguidance, Tabatabai holds, turn on whether one calls God by His Best Names or commits sacrilege in them [3]. The passage ends in light: a nation who guide by the truth, of whom Tusi says no age is ever left empty [15].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أَخْرَجَ مِنْ ظَهْرِ آدَمَ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَخَرَجُوا كَالذَّرِّ فَعَرَّفَهُمْ وَأَرَاهُمْ نَفْسَهُ وَلَوْ لا ذَلِكَ لَمْ يَعْرِفْ أَحَدٌ رَبَّهُ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: He brought out from Adam's back his descendants down to the Day of Resurrection, and they came out like particles. He made Himself known to them and showed them Himself; were it not for that, no one would know his Lord.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: إني كنت أول من آمن بربي، و أول من أجاب حين أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين و أشهدهم على أنفسهم: أ لست بربكم؟ قالوا: بلى. فكنت أنا أول نبي قال بلى، فسبقتهم بالإقرار بالله
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: I was the first to believe in my Lord and the first to answer when God took the covenant of the prophets and made them bear witness over themselves, 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes.' So I was the first prophet to say 'Yes,' and I outstripped them in acknowledging God.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كان الميثاق مأخوذاً عليهم لله بالربوبية ولرسوله بالنبوة ولأمير المؤمنين والأئمة بالإِمامة … فقال ألست بربكم ومحمد نبيكم وعلي إمامكم
narrations.chain: his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The covenant was taken from them for God as Lord, for His Messenger as prophet, and for the Commander of the Faithful and the Imams as imams. He said, 'Am I not your Lord, and Muhammad your prophet, and Ali your imam?'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الأصل في [ذلك] بلعم، ثم ضربه الله مثلا لكل مؤثر هواه على هدى الله من أهل القبلة

text.en: Originally this refers to Bal'am, then God made him a parable for everyone who prefers his own desire over God's guidance, from the people of the qibla.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: أنه أعطي بلعم بن باعورا الاسم الأعظم، فكان يدعو به فيستجاب له فمال إلى فرعون … فأنطقها الله عزوجل فقالت ويلك على ما تضربني أتريد أن أجيء معك لتدعو على موسى نبي الله وقوم مؤمنين، فلم يزل يضربها حتى قتلها وانسلخ الاسم الأعظم من لسانه
narrations.chain: his father, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida

text.en: Bal'am was given the Greatest Name, supplicating by it and being answered; then he inclined to Pharaoh. When he beat his she-donkey, God made it speak: 'Why beat me? Would you have me curse Musa, God's prophet, and a believing people?' He beat it until he killed it, and the Name left his tongue.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله تبارك وتعالى يضل الظالمين يوم القيامة عن دار كرامته، ويهدي أهل الإيمان والعمل الصالح إلى جنته
narrations.chain: Tamim ibn Bahlul, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Basri, from Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad

text.en: God leads the wrongdoers astray on the Day of Resurrection from the abode of His honor, and guides the people of faith and righteous deeds to His Paradise.

narrations.speaker: the Commander of the Faithful
narrations.arabic: أنّ الله ركّب في الملائكة عقلاً بلا شهوة وركّب في البهائم شهوة بلا عقل وركّب في بني آدم كلتيهما فمن غلب عقله شهوته فهوخير من الملائكة ومن غلب شهوته عقله فهو شرّ من البهائم

text.en: God placed in the angels intellect without desire, in the beasts desire without intellect, and in the children of Adam both. Whoever's intellect masters his desire is better than the angels, and whoever's desire masters his intellect is worse than the beasts.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: طبع الله عليها فلا تعقل … أي جعل في آذانهم و قرا فلن يسمعوا الهدى
narrations.chain: in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: God sealed their hearts, so they do not reason. And He put deafness in their ears, so they will not hear guidance.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نحن- و الله- الأسماء الحسنى التي لا يقبل الله من العباد إلا بمعرفتنا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: We, by God, are the Beautiful Names: God accepts nothing from the servants except through knowing us.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ الله (عَلَيْهِ السَّلام) عَنْ قَوْلِ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنا أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ قَالَ هُمُ الائِمَّةُ
narrations.chain: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: I asked Abu Abdillah about God's words, 'Among those We have created are a nation who guide by the truth and do justice thereby.' He said: They are the Imams.

narrations.speaker: the Commander of the Faithful
narrations.arabic: و الذي نفسي بيده لتفترقن هذه الأمة على ثلاث و سبعين فرقة كلها في النار إلا فرقة { وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ } فهذه التي تنجو من هذه الأمة
narrations.chain: from Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri, who heard the Commander of the Faithful

text.en: By Him in whose hand my soul is, this community will split into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire save one: 'Among those We have created are a nation who guide by the truth.' This is the one saved from this community.

perspectives.en: All read verse 172 as a covenant taken before birth: God drew the descendants of Adam from his loins as particles and had them testify that He is their Lord. Ibn Kathir binds this to the inborn fitra with which, in the Prophet's words, every child is born before its parents turn it to another creed [41], and Qurtubi cites the report from Umar that God then sorted the particles into people of Paradise and people of the Fire [47]. Shia narrations add a clause to the same covenant: alongside God's lordship the descendants also acknowledged the prophethood of Muhammad and the imamate of Ali and the Imams [16].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فإشهادهم على أنفسهم هو إراءتهم حقيقة أنفسهم ليتحملوا ما أُريد تحملهم من أمرها ثم يؤدوا ما تحملوه إذا سئلوا

sources.gloss: Making them witness over themselves is showing them the reality of their own selves, so that they carry what was intended of it and render it when asked.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: معنى إيتاء الآيات على ما يعطيه السياق التلبس من الآيات الأنفسية والكرامات الخاصة الباطنية بما يتنور به طريق معرفة الله له

sources.gloss: The meaning of giving him the signs, as the context yields, is his being clothed with inner signs and special hidden graces by which the path of knowing God was lit for him.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: أن الهدى والضلال يدوران مدار دعوته تعالى بأسمائه الحسنى والإِلحاد فيها

sources.gloss: Guidance and misguidance turn upon calling upon Him by His Best Names or committing sacrilege in them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: إنه مما يشهد ظاهر القرآن بخلافه لأنه تعالى قال وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم ولم يقل من آدم وقال من ظهوركم ولم يقل من ظهره وقال ذريتهم ولم يقل ذريته

sources.gloss: The apparent Qur'an testifies against it, for He said 'from the Children of Adam,' not 'from Adam,' 'from your loins,' not 'from his loin,' and 'their descendants,' not 'his descendant.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فقيل هو بلعام بن باعور عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود … أنه أمية ابن أبي الصلت الثقفي الشاعر

sources.gloss: It was said he is Bal'am ibn Ba'ur, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud … and that he is Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi, the poet.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: اللام في قولـه لجهنم لام العاقبة … يعني خلقناهم على أن عاقبتهم المصير إلى جهنم بكفرهم وإنكارهم وسوء اختيارهم

sources.gloss: The lam in 'for hell' is the lam of outcome … We created them such that their end is the passage to hell, by their disbelief, denial, and evil choice.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وبين أنه فعل ذلك بهم ليتوبوا وليرجعوا عن معاصيه الى طاعته وعن الكفر الى الايمان به

sources.gloss: He made clear that He did this to them so that they might repent and return from disobeying Him to obeying Him, and from disbelief to faith in Him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال ابو جعفر عليه السلام في الاصل بلعم ثم ضرب مثلا لكل مؤثر هواه على هدى الله تعالى من اهل القبلة

sources.gloss: Abu Ja'far said: originally it was Bal'am, then it was made a parable for everyone who prefers his desire over God's guidance, from the people of the qibla.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فشبهه بالكلب، لأن كل شيء يلهث فانما يلهث في حال الاعياء والكلال إلا الكلب فانه يلهث في حال الراحة والتعب

sources.gloss: He likened him to the dog, because everything that pants does so only in a state of fatigue and exhaustion, except the dog, which pants in ease and in weariness alike.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: عندنا انه لايخلوا وقت من الاوقات ممن يجب اتباعه وتثبت عصمته ويكون حجة الله على خلقه

sources.gloss: In our view, no time is ever without one whose following is obligatory, whose infallibility is established, and who is God's proof over His creation.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: كان الميثاق مأخوذاً عليهم لله بالربوبية ولرسوله بالنبوة ولأمير المؤمنين والأئمة بالإِمامة

sources.gloss: The covenant was taken from them for God as Lord, for His Messenger as prophet, and for the Commander of the Faithful and the Imams as imams.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أنه أعطي بلعم بن باعورا الاسم الأعظم، فكان يدعو به فيستجاب له فمال إلى فرعون

sources.gloss: Bal'am ibn Ba'ura was given the Greatest Name, and would supplicate by it and be answered, but he inclined to Pharaoh.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فكنت أنا أول نبي قال بلى، فسبقتهم بالإقرار بالله

sources.gloss: So I was the first prophet to say 'Yes,' and I outstripped them in acknowledging God.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الأصل في [ذلك] بلعم، ثم ضربه الله مثلا لكل مؤثر هواه على هدى الله من أهل القبلة

sources.gloss: Originally this refers to Bal'am, then God made him a parable for everyone who prefers his desire over God's guidance, from the people of the qibla.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: طبع الله عليها فلا تعقل … أي جعل في آذانهم و قرا فلن يسمعوا الهدى

sources.gloss: God sealed their hearts, so they do not reason … He put deafness in their ears, so they will not hear guidance.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نحن- و الله- الأسماء الحسنى التي لا يقبل الله من العباد إلا بمعرفتنا

sources.gloss: We, by God, are the Beautiful Names: God accepts nothing from the servants except through knowing us.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لتفترقن هذه الأمة على ثلاث و سبعين فرقة كلها في النار إلا فرقة … فهذه التي تنجو من هذه الأمة

sources.gloss: This community will split into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one … this is the one saved from this community.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أنّ الله ركّب في الملائكة عقلاً بلا شهوة وركّب في البهائم شهوة بلا عقل وركّب في بني آدم كلتيهما

sources.gloss: God placed in the angels intellect without desire, in the beasts desire without intellect, and in the children of Adam both.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: كل مولود يولد على الفطرة … فأبواه يهودانه وينصرانه ويمجسانه

sources.gloss: Every child is born upon the fitra … then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: إن الله تعالىٰ خلق آدم ثم مسح ظهره بيمينه فاستخرج منه ذُرِّية فقال خلقت هؤلاء للجنة وبعمل أهل الجنة يعملون ثم مسح ظهره فاستخرج منه ذُرِّية فقال خلقتُ هؤلاء للنار وبعمل أهل النار يعملون

sources.gloss: God created Adam, then wiped his back with His right hand and brought out a progeny, saying, 'I created these for Paradise and by the deeds of Paradise's people they act,' then wiped his back and brought out a progeny, saying, 'I created these for the Fire and by the deeds of the Fire's people they act.'

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: أَخْرَجَ مِنْ ظَهْرِ آدَمَ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَخَرَجُوا كَالذَّرِّ فَعَرَّفَهُمْ وَأَرَاهُمْ نَفْسَهُ وَلَوْ لا ذَلِكَ لَمْ يَعْرِفْ أَحَدٌ رَبَّهُ

sources.gloss: He brought out from Adam's back his descendants to the Day of Resurrection; they came out like particles, and He made Himself known to them and showed them Himself; were it not for that, no one would know his Lord.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: إن الله تبارك وتعالى يضل الظالمين يوم القيامة عن دار كرامته، ويهدي أهل الإيمان والعمل الصالح إلى جنته

sources.gloss: God leads the wrongdoers astray on the Day of Resurrection from the abode of His honor, and guides the people of faith and righteous deeds to His Paradise.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنا أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ قَالَ هُمُ الائِمَّةُ

sources.gloss: 'Among those We have created are a nation who guide by the truth and do justice thereby' - he said: They are the Imams.

essay.en:
This passage closes the surah's case against those who deny God's signs. To such deniers God promises no sudden blow but a slow undoing: He will draw them in imperceptibly and grant them respite, for His devising is sure. Tabrisi explains this 'drawing in' as being taken down step by step without warning [3], while Tusi rejects reading it as God pushing them into disbelief, which he holds would be a wrong contrary to God's wisdom [6].

The surah then answers the Meccans who called the Prophet mad. Let them reflect: there is no madness in their companion, who had stood on Safa warning Quraysh clan by clan only to be dismissed as a raving man; he is a plain warner [7]. And let them look into the dominion of the heavens and the earth and everything God has made, and weigh that their appointed time may be near - for reflection is a duty and blind imitation no substitute [7].

Whoever God leaves astray has no guide; He abandons them, bewildered, to their rebellion. When they demand to know when the Hour will arrive - a question the Jews and Quraysh pressed on him [4] - the Prophet is told to return its knowledge to God alone, for it weighs heavy on heaven and earth and comes only suddenly [2]. He must disclaim the Unseen entirely, owning neither benefit nor harm for himself except as God wills, and standing only as a warner and bearer of good news [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هو العبد يذنب الذنب فيملي له، و يجدد له عنده النعمة لتلهيه عن الاستغفار من الذنوب، فهو مستدرج من حيث لا يعلم
narrations.chain: From a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, together, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It is the servant who commits a sin, and is granted respite, and the blessing is renewed for him so that it distracts him from seeking forgiveness for his sins; so he is drawn in imperceptibly from where he does not know.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله إذا أراد بعبد خيرا فأذنب ذنبا أتبعه بنقمة و يذكره الاستغفار، و إذا أراد بعبد شرا فأذنب ذنبا أتبعه بنعمة لينسيه الاستغفار و يتمادى بها … بالنعم عند المعاصي
narrations.chain: From a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Samt, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When God intends good for a servant who then sins, He follows it with a punishment and reminds him to seek forgiveness; and when He intends evil for a servant who then sins, He follows it with a blessing to make him forget forgiveness and persist - drawing them in through blessings amid disobedience.

note.en: Here God's leaving them astray means He leaves the deniers to their rebellion and does not force them out of it; the straying is their own at His testing [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن الله عز و جل يقول في كتابه: { وَلَوْ كُنتُ أَعْلَمُ ٱلْغَيْبَ لاَسْتَكْثَرْتُ مِنَ ٱلْخَيْرِ وَمَا مَسَّنِيَ ٱلسُّوۤءُ } يعني الفقر
narrations.chain: al-Husayn ibn Bistam in Tibb al-A'imma, by his chain from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir

text.en: God says in His Book, 'Had I known the Unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no ill would have befallen me' - meaning poverty.

perspectives.en: On these verses the two traditions divide over free will. The Shia commentators insist that God's 'drawing in' and 'leading astray' cannot mean He creates the deniers' disbelief; Tusi calls that reading false and contrary to God's wisdom, holding rather that He leaves those who chose rebellion to themselves [6]. Razi and the Ash'aris read the same words the opposite way, taking 'drawing in,' 'respite,' and 'sure devising' as proof that God wills what drives the servant to disbelief [42]; and Qurtubi calls verse 186 a refutation of the Qadariyya, who deny that misguidance is from God [39].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان في الآيتين إبانة أن علم الساعة من الغيب المختص به تعالى لا يعلمه إلا الله، ولا دليل لتعيين وقتها والحدس لوقوعها أصلاً فلا تأتي إلا بغتة.

sources.gloss: These two verses make clear that knowledge of the Hour is among the Unseen belonging to God alone; none knows it but Him, there is no way to fix its time, and so it comes only suddenly.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: الاستدراج أصله من الدرجة وهو أن يؤخذ قليلاً قليلاً ولا يباغت

sources.gloss: istidraj (drawing in) is rooted in 'daraja' (a step): to be taken little by little, without being taken by surprise.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل جاء قوم من اليهود فقالوا يا محمد أخبرنا عن الساعة متى هي إن كنت نبيّاً فنزلت الآية عن ابن عباس. وقيل: قالت قريش يا محمد متى الساعة فنزلت الآية عن قتادة والحسن.

sources.gloss: It is said a group of Jews came and said, 'O Muhammad, tell us about the Hour, when is it, if you are a prophet,' and the verse was revealed (from Ibn Abbas); and it is said Quraysh said, 'O Muhammad, when is the Hour?' and it was revealed (from Qatada and al-Hasan).

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { لا أملك لنفسي نفعاً ولا ضراً إلا ما شاء الله } أن يملّكني إيّاه فأملكه بتمليكه إياي

sources.gloss: 'I have no control over benefit or harm for myself except what God wills' - that He grant me ownership of it, so that I own it only by His granting.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فأما من قال من المجبرة: إن معنى الآية أن الله يستدرجهم إلى الكفر والضلال فباطل، لأن الله تعالى لا يفعل ذلك لانه قبيح ينافي الحكمة

sources.gloss: As for those of the Mujbira who say the verse means God draws them to disbelief and error - that is false, for God does not do this, since it is a wrong that contradicts wisdom.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال الحسن وقتادة سبب نزول الآية ان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وقف على الصفا يدعوا قريشاً فخذاً فخذاً … وفي الآية دلالة على وجوب النظر وفساد التقليد

sources.gloss: al-Hasan and Qatada said the occasion of revelation was that the Prophet stood on al-Safa calling Quraysh clan by clan … and in the verse is proof of the obligation of reflection and the invalidity of blind imitation.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: { ويذرهم في طغيانهم } بمعنى يخلي بينهم وبين ذلك، وترك اخراجه بالقسر والجبر

sources.gloss: 'He leaves them in their rebellion' means He leaves them to it and refrains from forcing them out of it by compulsion.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هو العبد يذنب الذنب فيملي له، و يجدد له عنده النعمة لتلهيه عن الاستغفار من الذنوب، فهو مستدرج من حيث لا يعلم

sources.gloss: It is the servant who sins and is granted respite, and the blessing is renewed for him so that it distracts him from seeking forgiveness for his sins; so he is drawn in from where he does not know.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: { وَمَا مَسَّنِيَ ٱلسُّوۤءُ } يعني الفقر

sources.gloss: 'and no ill would have befallen me' - meaning poverty.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: بيّن أن إعراضهم لأن الله أضلّهم. وهذا ردّ على القدرية

sources.gloss: He made clear that their turning away is because God misled them; this is a refutation of the Qadariyya.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: أصحابنا احتجوا في مسألة القضاء والقدر بهذه الألفاظ الثلاثة، وهي الاستدراج والإملاء والكيد المتين، وكلها تدل على أنه تعالى أراد بالعبد ما يسوقه إلى الكفر

sources.gloss: Our companions [the Ash'aris] argued in the question of the divine decree from these three expressions - drawing in, respite, and sure devising - all of which indicate that God intended for the servant what drives him to disbelief.

essay.en:
Al-Mizan reads this closing passage as a return to the surah's running theme: the human being's covenant with his Lord and his breaking of it [1]. It opens with creation from a single soul and its mate, made so that he might find comfort with her; when the wife grows heavy with child, the two invoke God and vow that if He grants them a healthy child they will be grateful (189). Yet, once granted the child, they ascribe partners to Him. Majma al-Bayan and al-Tibyan read the single soul as Adam and its mate as Eve [3][9], while al-Mizan takes the two verses as a likeness struck for humankind: the parents who turn to God in need and forget Him once relieved [1].

From the ascribed partners the passage turns to argue against the idols. They create nothing and are themselves created; they can help neither their worshippers nor themselves; and if called to guidance they neither follow nor hear (191 to 198). Those the idolaters invoke are creatures like themselves, without feet, hands, eyes, or ears. The Prophet is told to answer that his sole guardian is God, who sent down the Book and takes care of the righteous.

The surah then schools the Prophet in conduct: adopt excusing, bid what is right, and turn away from the ignorant (199). When this came and he asked how to bear anger, the verse on Satan's disturbance was revealed, teaching him to seek God's protection [6] (200). The Godwary, when a visitation of Satan touches them, remember and see clearly, while others' brethren drag them deeper into error (201 to 202). To those who demand a sign he answers that he follows only what is revealed, and that the Quran is insight, guidance, and mercy (203).

The passage ends in worship: listen in silence when the Quran is recited, which Majma al-Bayan holds to apply chiefly to prayer behind the imam [8] (204), and remember your Lord within the heart, morning and evening, not aloud (205). It closes with those near their Lord, who never disdain to worship Him, glorify Him, and prostrate: the first prostration of the Quran [23] (206).

note.en: Al-Mizan keeps the prophet Adam free of this shirk by reading verses 189 and 190 as a parable for humankind, not a report of two individuals [1].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إن حواء ولدت لآدم (عليه السلام) خمس مائة بطن، في كل بطن ذكر و أنثى … فجعل الصنفان لله تعالى ذكره شركاء فيما آتاهما، و لم يشكراه كشكر أبويهما له عز و جل
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Tamim ibn Abdillah al-Qurashi, from his father, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Jahm

text.en: Eve bore Adam five hundred births, each with a male and a female. Adam and Eve covenanted with God and prayed. When He gave them sound offspring, the two kinds, males and females, ascribed partners to God in what He gave, and did not thank Him as their parents had.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هما آدم وحوّاء وانّما كان شركهما شرك طاعة وليس شرك عبادة … جعلا للحارث نصيباً في خلق الله ولم يكن أشركا إبليس في عبادة الله

text.en: They are Adam and Eve. Their associating was an associating of obedience, not of worship. They gave al-Harith a share in God's creation, yet they did not make Iblis a partner in the worship of God.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ألا و إن مكارم الدنيا و الآخرة في ثلاثة أحرف من كتاب الله عز و جل: { خُذِ ٱلْعَفْوَ وَأْمُرْ بِٱلْعُرْفِ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ ٱلْجَاهِلِينَ } ، و تفسيره أن تصل من قطعك، و تعفو عمن ظلمك، و تعطي من حرمك
narrations.chain: al-Shaykh in his Majalis, from al-Husayn ibn Ubaydillah, from Harun ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ma'mar, from Hamdan ibn al-Mu'afa, from Hamawayh ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Isa al-Alawi

text.en: The noble traits of this world and the next lie in three phrases from the Book of God: 'Adopt excusing, bid what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.' Its meaning is that you join whoever cut you off, pardon whoever wronged you, and give whoever deprived you.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هو العبد يهم بالذنب ثم يتذكر فيمسك، فذلك قوله: { تَذَكَّرُواْ فَإِذَا هُم مُّبْصِرُونَ }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ashari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fadal, from Thalaba ibn Maymun, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It is the servant who resolves upon a sin, then remembers and holds back. That is His words, 'they remember, and behold, they perceive.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: و إن كنت خلف إمام فلا تقرأن شيئا في الأوليين، و أنصت لقراءته … فإن الله عز و جل يقول: { وَإِذَا قُرِىءَ ٱلْقُرْآنُ } يعني في الفريضة خلف الإمام { فَٱسْتَمِعُواْ لَهُ وَأَنصِتُواْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ }
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh in al-Faqih, by his chain, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: If you are behind an imam, do not recite anything in the first two rak'as, and be silent for his recitation. God's words 'When the Quran is recited' mean in the obligatory prayer behind the imam, 'listen to it and be silent.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir or al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا يكتب الملك إلا ما سمع، و قال الله عز و جل: { وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعاً وَخِيفَةً } و لا يعلم ثواب ذلك الذكر في نفس الرجل غير الله عز و جل لعظمته
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams

text.en: The angel writes down only what he hears. God said, 'Remember your Lord within your heart, beseechingly and reverentially.' None but God knows the reward of that remembrance within a man's soul, for its greatness.

note.en: Al-Tibyan reads 'those near your Lord' as the angels, near in rank not place; Tafsir al-Qummi, as the prophets and Imams. It is the Quran's first, recommended prostration [23][32].

perspectives.en: Shia and Sunni exegetes part ways on verse 190. The Shia sources guard the prophet Adam's infallibility: al-Mizan treats the two verses as a parable for humankind, not a report about Adam and Eve [1], and Imam al-Rida told al-Ma'mun that the partners were ascribed by the couple's many descendants, not by the parents, who had thanked God [33]. Sunni tafsirs instead relate, on Samura's authority from the Prophet, that Iblis deceived Adam and Eve into naming their child 'Abd al-Harith' [61][91]. Al-Razi, himself a Sunni, rejects that story as incompatible with Adam's knowledge [80].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: الكلام في الآيتين جار مجرى المثل المضروب لبني آدم في نقضهم موثقهم الذي واثقوه، وظلمهم بآيات الله.

sources.gloss: The discourse in the two verses runs as a likeness struck for the sons of Adam, in their breaking the covenant they had made and their wronging by the signs of God.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { من نفس واحدة } يعني آدم ع … { منها زوجها } يعني حواء

sources.gloss: 'From a single soul' means Adam; 'from it its mate' means Eve.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: خلق البشر من نفس واحدة وهي آدم وخلق منها زوجها يعني حواء

sources.gloss: He created mankind from a single soul, which is Adam, and created from it its mate, meaning Eve.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال ابن زيد: لما نزلت هذه الآية قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: كيف يا رب والغضب فنزل قولـه { وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ }

sources.gloss: Ibn Zayd said: when this verse was revealed the Prophet said, 'How, my Lord, with anger?' so 'Should a temptation from Satan disturb you' came down.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أقوى الأقوال الأول لأنه لا حال يجب فيها الإنصات لقراءة القرآن إلا حالة قراءة الإمام في الصلاة

sources.gloss: The strongest view is the first, for there is no state in which silence for the Quran's recitation is obligatory except during the imam's recitation in prayer.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ان الذين عنده، وهم الملائكة … وهذا اول سجدات القرآن، وهي - عندنا - مستحبة غير واجبة

sources.gloss: Those with Him are the angels ... and this is the first of the Quran's prostrations, which for us is recommended, not obligatory.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: { إن الذين عند ربك } يعني الأنبياء والرسل والأئمة عليهم السلام

sources.gloss: 'Indeed those who are near your Lord' means the prophets, the messengers, and the Imams.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن حواء ولدت لآدم (عليه السلام) خمس مائة بطن، في كل بطن ذكر و أنثى … فجعل الصنفان لله تعالى ذكره شركاء فيما آتاهما، و لم يشكراه كشكر أبويهما

sources.gloss: Eve bore Adam five hundred births, in each a male and a female ... so the two kinds ascribed partners to God in what He gave them, and did not thank Him as their parents did.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن مكارم الدنيا و الآخرة في ثلاثة أحرف من كتاب الله عز و جل … و تفسيره أن تصل من قطعك، و تعفو عمن ظلمك، و تعطي من حرمك

sources.gloss: The noble traits of this world and the next are in three phrases from the Book of God ... its meaning is that you join whoever cut you off, pardon whoever wronged you, and give whoever deprived you.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هو العبد يهم بالذنب ثم يتذكر فيمسك

sources.gloss: It is the servant who resolves upon a sin, then remembers and holds back.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و إن كنت خلف إمام فلا تقرأن شيئا في الأوليين، و أنصت لقراءته … يعني في الفريضة خلف الإمام

sources.gloss: If you are behind an imam, do not recite anything in the first two rak'as, and be silent for his recitation ... meaning in the obligatory prayer behind the imam.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لا يكتب الملك إلا ما سمع … و لا يعلم ثواب ذلك الذكر في نفس الرجل غير الله عز و جل لعظمته

sources.gloss: The angel writes down only what he hears ... and none but God knows the reward of that remembrance within a man's soul, because of its greatness.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: هما آدم وحوّاء وانّما كان شركهما شرك طاعة وليس شرك عبادة

sources.gloss: They are Adam and Eve, and their associating was an associating of obedience, not an associating of worship.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: لما ولدت حواء، طاف بها إبليس، وكان لا يعيش لها ولد، فقال سميه عبد الحارث، فإنه يعيش، فسمته عبد الحارث، فعاش، وكان ذلك من وحي الشيطان وأمره

sources.gloss: When Eve gave birth, Iblis went about her, since no child of hers had survived, and said, 'Name him Abd al-Harith and he will live.' She named him Abd al-Harith, and he lived; that was from Satan's suggestion and command.

sources.author: Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti

excerpt.text: لما ولدت حواء طاف بها إبليس وكان لا يعيش لها ولد، فقال: سميه عبد الحارث فإنه يعيش، فسمته عبد الحارث فعاش، فكان ذلك من وحي الشيطان وأمره

sources.gloss: When Eve gave birth, Iblis went about her, since no child of hers had survived, and said, 'Name him Abd al-Harith and he will live.' She named him Abd al-Harith, and he lived; that was from Satan's suggestion and command.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: واعلم أن هذا التأويل فاسد ويدل عليه وجوه

sources.gloss: Know that this interpretation is false, and several proofs indicate it.
